### The project code pytest loads as plugins is judged by the hook and CI (item 156)

Wrong-verdict note. In v2.0.0 (`nucleo/src/lang.rs`'s Python profile, `git tag --contains 4f9d784`, the oldest tag): the Python globs lock the `conftest.py` files present at RED, but not a `conftest.py` added during GREEN, nor the project modules pytest imports as plugins before the tests (named by `-p` in `addopts` or in the suite's command, or by `pytest_plugins` in a `conftest.py`). A GREEN that edits such a module, or adds a `conftest.py`, can make a locked failing case report as passed. Recorded as a later item by item 138's spec (commit `9f77559`, 2026-11-19T21:02:21-03:00, its "Known limits": "A local plugin named by `-p` in `addopts` and present at RED ... is not locked"). The layer that should have caught it is section 1's guarantee ("its support files, or the config that says how the suite runs"): item 138 judged pytest's settings but left the code they load to the globs, and the globs see neither a module outside them nor a file added after RED.

**Reproduction, on main (2.90.0, built from `bc2ba75`):** scratch repositories with real pytest 8.4.2 in a virtual environment and the Python config `init` writes, its suite command `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider --junitxml={junit}`, each with one failing case `tests/test_calc.py::test_adds` against a stub `calc.py` whose `add` raises `NotImplementedError`, and one passing case. `red` locks 2 files (`.shipcraft.toml`, `tests/test_calc.py`). In each, a GREEN commit that changes only the file named below, to a `pytest_runtest_makereport` hook wrapper that turns a failed report into a passed one, leaves `calc.py` raising, passes the hook (`all locked cases pass`) and closes the lock:
- (A) `pytest.ini` with `addopts = -p myplugin` and a tracked `myplugin.py` at RED; the GREEN edits `myplugin.py`;
- (B) a root `conftest.py` (globs `tests/**`, so not locked) with `pytest_plugins = ["helpers.plug"]` and a tracked `helpers/plug.py`; the GREEN edits `helpers/plug.py`;
- (C) `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`, `pythonpath = ["plugins"]` and `addopts = "-p myplug"`, and a tracked `plugins/myplug.py`; the GREEN edits `plugins/myplug.py`;
- (D) `-p cmdplug` in the suite's command and a tracked `cmdplug.py`; the GREEN edits `cmdplug.py`;
- (E) the globs `tests/**` and `**/conftest.py`, no `conftest.py` at RED; the GREEN adds a root `conftest.py`.

The first RED case reproduces (A) on main: it fails on 2.90.0 because the hook accepts the commit.

Everything in items 13, 15c, 43, 46, 98, 132 and 138 holds unless a point below changes it: the lock and its format, `red` and `red --redo` (their output, the lock's `files` and every refusal), the selection, the controls, item 138's check (its watched paths, settings, lines and order) and every existing refusal code. Only the hook and CI change: item 138's check gains a second part and one refusal.

**How pytest loads project code before the tests, and what this item judges.** From pytest's documentation ("Writing plugins", "Plugin discovery order at tool startup", "Configuration") and its source (`_pytest/config/__init__.py`: `consider_preparse`, `consider_env`, `consider_conftest`, `consider_module`, `_getconftestmodules`; `_pytest/python_path.py`):

| Way | Judged here | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `-p <name>` in `addopts` of a config file (and `-p<name>`) | yes, point 1 | read from the settings item 138 already watches |
| `-o addopts=...` and `-o pythonpath=...` (`--override-ini`) in the command or in `addopts` | yes, point 1 | the same names and folders, given on the command line |
| `-p <name>` in the suite's `command` | yes, point 1 | the command is in `.shipcraft.toml`, which every lock holds |
| `conftest.py` files | yes, point 1, every one the suite watches, also one added during GREEN | pytest imports them before collecting the tests |
| `pytest_plugins` in a `conftest.py` or in a judged plugin module | yes, point 1, read leniently (string literals only) | the names are in judged files |
| `pythonpath` entries | only as folders where a plugin name resolves (point 1), and a symbolic link on the way is judged | the whole folder is usually the product (`pythonpath = ["src"]`, the src layout); locking it would refuse every GREEN |
| `confcutdir`, `rootdir`, `--import-mode` and other settings | already item 138's (`pytest-config-changed`) | they are settings, not code |
| `-p` given by a wrapper (`tox.ini`'s `commands`, a script the command runs) | no, known limit | item 138 does not treat a wrapper as a pytest suite |
| `PYTEST_PLUGINS` and `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` in the environment | no, known limit | not in the repository |
| `pytest11` entry points of installed distributions (the project's own included) | no, known limit | installed code; for a pytest plugin project the entry-point module is the product itself |
| `pytest_plugins` in a test module | no, known limit | finding it means reading every test file on every commit; the test module itself is locked |
| what a plugin module or `conftest.py` imports (`from helpers import x`), and the package `__init__.py` files pytest imports along a `conftest.py` or a test module | no, known limit | pytest registers no hooks from them: it is ordinary imported code, like the product, which can patch pytest just as well (first known limit) |
| a `cd <dir> &&` or another shell step in the command | no, known limit | the command's working folder is taken as the suite's root |
| an `@file` argument file named in the command (its `-o` lines) | no, known limit | reading it needs its own reader and failure rules; the file sits in the repository, so a later item can judge it |

1. **pytest's plugin files of a snapshot.** For every pytest suite of the judged snapshot's `.shipcraft.toml` (item 138's: `command` contains `pytest`; with none, nothing changes), read in the snapshot and in each parent (each a *source snapshot*):
   - **Conftest files.** A *watched conftest* is a path named exactly `conftest.py` that the suite *holds* (item 138's rule: under the suite's root at any depth, or directly in a folder from the repository root down to the root's parent).
   - **Bases.** The folders where a plugin name resolves: the suite's root (`""` for the project's root; `python -m pytest` puts it on `sys.path`); and, for each `pythonpath` value read from a watched path of item 138 present in the source snapshot, each entry joined to that config file's folder (`.` and empty segments dropped, each `..` removing the segment before it; an entry that starts with `/` or climbs above the repository root is no base).
   - **Plugin names.**
     - `-p` in arguments: in a list of arguments, an argument exactly `-p` names the next argument (none when it is the last), and an argument that starts with `-p` and is longer names the rest (`-pmyplugin`); the name is trimmed of whitespace (Rust's `str::trim`), and one that starts with `no:` (`-p no:cacheprovider`, which blocks a plugin) names nothing. This is pytest's `consider_preparse`.
     - `-o` in arguments: an argument exactly `-o` or `--override-ini` gives the next argument (nothing when it is the last), one that starts with `--override-ini=` gives the text after that `=`, and any other that starts with `-o` and is longer gives the rest. The given text, cut at its first `=`, is a key (trimmed) and a value (nothing without `=`). Key `addopts`: the value, split, is one more list read for `-p` (not for `-o` again). Key `pythonpath`: the value, split, gives entries joined (as below) to the suite's root and to the folder of each watched path of item 138 present in the source snapshot.
     - The suite's `command`, split as below, is one list, read for `-p` and `-o`.
     - The `addopts` value of each watched path of item 138 present in the source snapshot and not a symbolic link is one list. In `pytest.ini` and `.pytest.ini` the value is read from the `[pytest]` section, in `setup.cfg` from `[tool:pytest]`, in `tox.ini` from `[pytest]` (item 138's section scanner); in `pytest.toml` and `.pytest.toml` from the `pytest` table, and in `pyproject.toml` from both `tool.pytest.ini_options` and `tool.pytest` (each a list), parsed as item 138 parses them (a file that does not parse names nothing). Each list is read for `-p` and `-o`.
     - `pythonpath` is read from the same places as `addopts`, and its value split the same way.
     - **An INI value.** Inside item 138's section text (its lines, separators and headers as item 138 reads them, kept as they are, though newer `iniconfig` releases reject some of those separators), each line is classified as `iniconfig` 2.x classifies it: a line that is empty after trimming (Rust's `str::trim`), or whose trimmed text starts with `#` or `;`, is skipped and ends nothing; a line that starts with whitespace (Rust's `char::is_whitespace`), or that starts with `[` and is not a header, continues the current value, its trimmed text appended after a `\n`; a header ends the current value; any other line is a key line, ending the current value: its key is the text before its first `=` or `:`, trimmed, and its value the text after it, trimmed (a line with neither, which pytest refuses, starts no value). Every key line named `addopts` (or `pythonpath`) counts, also a repeated one (pytest refuses a repeated key; the reader takes both).
     - **A TOML value.** A string is split as below; an array gives each of its string elements as one argument, and skips the others; any other value names nothing. This is lenient on purpose: pytest 9's native `[tool.pytest]` and `pytest.toml` options want typed lists, and the reader also takes a string there.
     - **The split** is Python's `shlex.split` (POSIX mode, no comments): space, tab, CR and LF separate arguments; `'...'` is literal; inside `"..."` a backslash escapes only `"` and `\`; outside quotes a backslash escapes the next character. A text with an unclosed quote or a trailing backslash is split on whitespace instead (pytest itself fails on it).
     - **`pytest_plugins`.** Each watched conftest present in the source snapshot, and each plugin file of this point found there that ends in `.py`, is read with `Repo::read` (lossy UTF-8) unless it is a symbolic link, and scanned as Python text, its lines split at LF, CRLF and CR (Python's physical lines; each CRLF and lone CR read as an LF, the end of the file ending the last line). `#` to the end of the line is a comment. A *string literal* is an optional run of ASCII letters directly before `'`, `"`, `'''` or `"""`, through the matching closing quote, a backslash escaping the next character; a one-quote literal ends at the end of its line when it is not closed there, and a triple-quoted one may span lines. Outside comments and string literals, an *assignment* is the word `pytest_plugins` at the start of a line (column 0, the next character not an ASCII letter, digit or `_`), then optional spaces and tabs, then `=` not followed by `=`, or `:` followed by an annotation that ends at the first `=` not followed by `=` outside string literals and brackets on that line (none: no assignment). The *value* starts after that `=`. A *plain literal* is a string literal with no prefix, not triple-quoted and with no backslash. After optional spaces and tabs, a value is read when it is:
       - one plain literal followed only by spaces, tabs, an optional comment and the end of the line: its names are its content split at `,`, parts not trimmed (pytest splits a string value at commas and imports each part as it is);
       - `(`, one plain literal and `)` with no comma, with spaces, tabs, line ends and comments around the literal, followed only by spaces, tabs, an optional comment and the end of the line: a grouped string, read as the first form (`("a,b")` gives `a` and `b`);
       - `[` or `(`, then plain literals separated by commas, one trailing comma allowed, with spaces, tabs, line ends and comments around them, then the matching `]` or `)`, followed only by spaces, tabs, an optional comment and the end of the line (or of the file): each literal's content, not trimmed, is one name.
       Any other value names nothing: a variable, a call, a concatenation (`["a"] + ["b"]`), a nested bracket, a literal with a prefix, triple quotes or a backslash, a sequence not closed before the end of the file. Every assignment in a file counts.
   - **Candidates.** A name is *valid* when, split at `.`, every part is non-empty and made only of ASCII letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit; an invalid name has no candidates. For a valid name `a.b.c` and a base `B` (`B/` stands for nothing when `B` is `""`), the candidates are each package's `B/a/__init__.py` and `B/a/b/__init__.py`, the module `B/a/b/c.py` and the package `B/a/b/c/__init__.py`. Every name is tried in every base; for a name read from a Python file, that file's folder is a base too, and so is, for each watched conftest present in the source snapshot, its *package root*: starting at the conftest's folder, while that folder holds an `__init__.py` that is a path of the source snapshot, go up one folder; the folder reached (`""` at the repository root) is the package root, which pytest's default import mode puts on `sys.path` to import the conftest as a package module. Names and bases are pooled across the pytest suites of the config, per source snapshot.
   - **Linked folders.** Each folder on a candidate's path (`svc` and `svc/a` for `svc/a/b.py`) that is a path of the source snapshot with git mode `120000` (a symbolic link to a folder, which git lists as one path) is a plugin file too, so it is judged as linked: a `pythonpath = ["plugins"]` whose `plugins` is a link to `realplugins` would otherwise let an edit of `realplugins/myplugin.py` through.
   - **Plugin files.** The source snapshots are the judged snapshot and its parents (not their parents). The plugin files of a source snapshot are its watched conftests, the linked folders, and the candidates of its names that are paths of the judged snapshot or of a parent, found to the end (a candidate present in the source snapshot is read for `pytest_plugins` in turn, each file once per source snapshot), so the result does not depend on the order of reading. Discovery of every source snapshot ends before point 2 compares anything, so a read failure in it (exit 2) wins over a refusal.
   - **The judged paths** are the plugin files of every source snapshot, each once, in bytewise order, without the paths in the lock's `files` (`check_files` judges those by hash, so an edited locked `conftest.py` stays `test-changed`, and a `conftest.py` a redo adds to the lock is not judged here). The exclusion applies to the comparison only: a locked `conftest.py` is still read, and the plugins it names are judged.
2. **The hook and CI refuse a change to a plugin file while a lock is open.** Item 138's check, right after its settings part accepts (so a commit that changes both is refused `pytest-config-changed`, as today), judges the paths of point 1 in bytewise order with item 138's comparison, the *code* of a path being: *none* when absent from a snapshot; *linked* (equal to nothing) when it is a symbolic link there (git mode `120000`); else its bytes, read with `Repo::read`. It refuses, with code `pytest-plugin-changed`, the first path whose code in the snapshot equals that of no parent:
   `shipcraft refused: pytest's plugins in <path> <done> <place> with lock <lock> open`
   `Why: pytest loads this file as plugin code before the tests (its hooks can skip, deselect or pass a case), so changing it during GREEN changes the judge mid-game`
   `Next: undo the change to pytest's plugins in <path>; if the suite needs it, make it after the cycle closes`
   `<done>`, `<place>`, `<path>` and `<lock>` are item 138's (`are behind a symbolic link`, `were added`, `were removed`, `changed`; `snapshot.describe()`; `red::one_line`), and so are the hook and CI places, the bound locks' order, the merge rule (a merge whose code equals one parent's is accepted), the closing commit (`Closed` judged like any commit that is not `Opened`), the RED commit (`Opened`, not judged: the RED may add or change plugin files with its tests) and the read failures (a `Repo::read` or listing failure: exit 2). The check runs before the suite. This refuses (A) to (E).
   - Only the files of point 1 are judged: a GREEN that changes a module no plugin name reaches, or `calc.py` itself, is accepted, and so is a new test file (section "GREEN may add tests"), but a new `conftest.py` the suite watches is refused, as item 132 refuses an added runner config.

This is the stricter path, applied without a lock change, as item 138 applies it (and, like item 138's, it accepts that a file pytest would not load is judged: RULES.md rule 2's exception, counted by the metric): a parent-by-parent comparison catches a plugin file added (a module that would shadow a judged name in an earlier base, a `myplugin/__init__.py` beside `myplugin.py`), edited or removed, needs no migration, and judges locks written before this release. Locking the files at RED instead would miss a `conftest.py` added after it, and locking the `pythonpath` folders would lock the product.

**Existing locks and configs.** No migration, no new lock key, no new format: `red`'s output and the lock it writes are byte for byte today's. Point 2 applies to every open lock, old or new. `init` writes the same globs and config.

**The version: 2.91.0.** A fix, but not a patch: it adds a refusal code (`pytest-plugin-changed`), and a GREEN that changes a plugin file is refused where 2.90.0 accepted it. Nothing breaks a config, a lock or a command, so it is minor. `init` writes `shipcraft_min = "2.91"`; existing configs keep theirs. Items in flight may take this number first; the item then takes the next free minor, in section 11 and `nucleo/Cargo.toml` alike, after its lock closes.

**Known limits.**
- The ways the table marks "no": a wrapper's `-p`, the environment, entry points, `pytest_plugins` in a test module, and code a plugin file imports. Product code imported by the tests also runs inside pytest's process and could patch it; no lock reaches that, and the review is the layer.
- A `pytest_plugins` value point 1 does not read (a variable, a comprehension, a concatenation, a nested bracket, a prefixed, triple-quoted or escaped literal such as `r"x"` or `"plug\x69n"`) names nothing; a name that is not ASCII, a compiled module (`.so`, `.pyc`) and a namespace package's other folders are not candidates; a `pytest_plugins` string part with spaces (`"a, b"` gives `a` and ` b`) is not a valid name, as pytest cannot import it either.
- A `-o pythonpath=...` entry is joined to every folder it could be relative to (the suite's root and each watched config's folder), not only the one pytest picks.
- A submodule (git mode `160000`) on a candidate's path is not followed.
- An `@file` argument in the command is not read, so an `-o pythonpath=...` or `-o addopts=...` in it gives nothing.
- The package root is computed for the watched conftests only, with the default (`prepend`) import mode's rule; `--import-mode=append` or `importlib` and a test module's package root are not followed.
- Every watched config's `addopts` and `pythonpath` is read, also one pytest does not select (item 138's stricter path), and every name is tried in every base, also where Python would not look (a base that is not on `sys.path` for a plain `pytest` run): a file that only shares a plugin's name is judged. The metric counts it.
- A project whose product is the plugin it loads with `-p` (a pytest plugin tested in the outer run instead of through `pytester` or an entry point) gets `pytest-plugin-changed` on every GREEN that changes it; such a project names the plugin through an entry point.
- A watched `conftest.py` that is a symbolic link is refused on every GREEN commit that holds it while a lock is open, as item 138 refuses a linked `pytest.ini`.
- A suite command is split as `shlex.split` splits it: `$VAR`, `$(...)`, a `cd <dir> &&` before pytest and a `-p` inside `sh -c "..."` are not followed; the command's working folder is taken as the suite's root.
- Item 141's paragraph says its per-commit check reads no `.shipcraft.toml`, while `ci`'s per-commit checks (items 132, 138, 140 and this one) read the judged snapshot's config with `Config::at`; this item keeps today's code and leaves that sentence to a later item.
- The check runs only where 2.91.0 runs: a project whose hook or CI uses an older binary is not protected until it upgrades.

**Metric:** on the release, the reproduction's (A) to (E) GREEN commits are refused `pytest-plugin-changed` with real pytest. False refusals: GREEN commits refused `pytest-plugin-changed` where the change was not a test shortcut (a new `conftest.py` with fixtures for new tests, a file that only shares a plugin's name), counted from each refused commit, over the first 10 such refusals in any project we run (POC-051's Python runs included). Revert: above 1 false refusal in those 10, a release drops the added-`conftest.py` and shadowing routes (judging only paths present in a parent) and lists them as a known limit.

**Current behavior** on these paths (keep unless marked change):
- `check`'s hook path calls, for each bound lock, `check_files`, then (not `Opened`) `check_lefthook`, `vitest_files::check_added`, `pytest_config::check_changed` and `jest_files::check_changed`, then runs the suite; `ci` makes the same calls per commit of `<base>..HEAD`, and `close`'s per-commit check (item 141) reuses `ci`'s. Change: `pytest_config::check_changed` also takes the lock (for its `files`) and gains point 2 after its settings part; nothing else moves.
- `pytest_config::check_changed` reads the snapshot's config with `Config::at` (nothing when absent), takes the pytest suites, and refuses `pytest-config-changed` on the first changed setting. Keep, byte for byte, before point 2.
- `check_files` judges every path in the lock's `files` by hash (`locked-file-deleted`, `config-changed`, `test-changed`). Keep.
- `red` and `red --redo`: the lock's `files`, their output lines and refusals. Keep, byte for byte.
- `check::run`, before the per-lock checks, refuses a legacy config, warns about locks outside, removes the close mark on `--commit-msg`, validates the staged config and judges the lock transitions; with no bound lock it prints `shipcraft: no open lock; commit allowed.` and stops. Keep.
- Standing effects the cases can meet, all kept: the run-log rows (the hook writes a row on every commit; a refusal's row carries its code), the close-mark and post-commit close flow, and the suite running in the tree or an export of the index, as item 132's "Current behavior" lists them.
- `close` without a close mark on a HEAD the hook did not judge (item 141, `unjudged::post_commit`): it runs `ci`'s per-commit check and prints its verdict line (refused or failure), always exits 0, writes no row and changes nothing, on every invocation. Change: the verdict can now be a `pytest-plugin-changed` refusal; everything else kept.
- Items 139 and 149's output capture: the first command a hook or CI run starts creates or truncates the worktree's `shipcraft/output/hook.log` or `ci.log`; a refusal before any command leaves the old file untouched, and a failure to write it changes no exit code. Keep: point 2 refuses before the suite, as item 138's check does.

### The files Jest reads beside the tests are locked, and its `package.json` key is judged (item 140)

Wrong-verdict note. In v2.0.0 (`nucleo/src/lang.rs`'s Node profile, `git tag --contains 4f9d784`, the oldest tag: `init` writes the `jest` command and the glob `**/jest.config.*`): the Node globs lock `jest.config.*` but not the files a Jest config names (`setupFiles`, `setupFilesAfterEnv`, `globalSetup`, `globalTeardown`), nor the `jest` key of `package.json`, where Jest reads the same settings. Recorded as a later item by item 132's spec (its "Known limits") and reproduced by item 138's spec (commit `9f77559`, 2026-11-19T21:02:21-03:00, its "Known limits"). The layer that should have caught it is section 1's guarantee ("its support files, or the config that says how the suite runs"); item 132 closed it for vitest only.

**Reproduction, on main (2.80.0, the shared binary):** scratch repositories with real Jest 30 (npm `jest@30.2.0`, `jest-junit@16.0.0`) and `init --lang node`'s config (runner `jest`, 2.0.0's globs), each with one failing case `src/sum.test.js:: adds` against a stub `src/sum.js` whose `sum` throws, and one passing case. Each GREEN commit below leaves `src/sum.js` throwing, passes the hook (`all locked cases pass`) and closes the lock:
- (A) `jest.config.js` with `setupFiles: ["<rootDir>/src/setup.js"]` at RED. `red` locks 4 files (`.shipcraft.toml`, `jest.config.js`, `src/other.test.js`, `src/sum.test.js`). The GREEN changes only `src/setup.js`, to `jest.mock("./sum", () => ({ sum: () => 3 }))`.
- (B) `package.json` with `"jest": {"setupFilesAfterEnv": ["<rootDir>/src/after.js"]}` at RED. `red` locks 3 files (`.shipcraft.toml` and the two test files). The GREEN changes only `src/after.js`, to the same mock.
- (C) `package.json` with no `jest` key at RED. The GREEN adds `"jest": {"moduleNameMapper": {"^\\./sum$": "<rootDir>/src/fake.js"}}` and a new `src/fake.js` whose `sum` returns 3.
- (D) no Jest config at RED. The GREEN adds `jest.config.js` with `setupFiles: ["./src/boot.js"]` and a new `src/boot.js` with the same mock.

The first RED case reproduces (A) on main: it fails on 2.80.0 because the hook accepts the commit.

Everything in items 13, 15c, 43, 46, 53, 55, 60, 65, 98, 132 and 138 holds unless a point below changes it: what the hook and CI judge (every path in the lock's `files`, by hash), the existing refusal codes, the lock format, the selection, the controls and the second run. Item 132's rules for vitest suites are unchanged byte for byte. `red` and `red --redo` hash more paths into `files` for Jest suites and can refuse `setup-unreadable` for them; item 132's line names Jest; the hook and CI refuse an added Jest config (`runner-config-added`) and gain one refusal, `jest-config-changed`.

1. **`red` locks the Jest configs, the modules they import and the setup files they name.**
   - **Which suites.** A *Jest suite* is a suite whose `command` contains `jest` (the substring test item 132 uses for `vitest`). For a suite that is neither a vitest nor a Jest suite nothing changes. A suite whose command contains both is both. Paths found through several suites or both runners are locked once.
   - **Jest configs.** A *Jest config name* is a last path component `jest.config.<ext>`, `<ext>` one of `ts`, `mts`, `cts`, `js`, `mjs`, `cjs`, `json`. A *candidate* is a path of `repo.files()` with no path component `node_modules` and a Jest config name. Jest looks for its config in the folder it runs from and in the folders above it, so the *locked Jest configs* of a Jest suite are the candidates under the suite's root at any depth (every candidate when the root is the project's), and the candidates directly in a folder that holds the root (each folder from the repository root down to the root's parent; a sibling folder of the root is not one). This is item 138's watched-path rule with Jest's names.
   - **Manifests.** A *watched manifest* of a Jest suite is a path of `repo.files()` named `package.json`, with no component `node_modules`, under the suite's root at any depth or directly in a folder that holds the root (the same rule). Point 1 adds no manifest to the lock: the hook and CI judge its `jest` key instead (point 4), as item 138 judges `pyproject.toml`'s table without locking the manifest. A manifest the suite's own globs match (`globs = ["tests/**", "package.json"]`) is locked as a test file, as today; so is a setup file the globs match.
   - **Config modules and the scan.** The locked Jest configs are config modules, and every path reached from one through a relative import is one, exactly as item 132 defines them (the same scan, imports resolved from the importing module's own folder, `.json` modules reached by an import locked but not scanned, a bare import not followed). A Jest config whose own extension is `json` (`jest.config.json`), and a `.json` module reached by an import from a Jest config module (`require('./config/options.json')`), are not scanned: they are read with the JSON reader below, as an options object (the whole document, which must be a JSON object, else `it is not a JSON object`; a document that is not UTF-8 or not JSON is unreadable the same way). A `jest.config.json` is parsed as Jest parses it, with comments allowed: through `jsonc::parse`, Shipcraft's JSONC reader (item 16b; it also takes a trailing comma and a BOM, which Jest would refuse itself). An imported `.json` module is parsed strictly, as Node's `require` does (`serde_json`). The root folder of an imported `.json` module is the root folder of the Jest config that reached it, like any imported module, and a `rootDir` in it is unreadable (`it sets rootDir`); only a Jest config file (`jest.config.json` included) and a manifest's `jest` object set the root folder. For a relative import from a Jest config module, the candidates are item 132's followed by the path with `.json` (Node's `require('./config/options')` finds `config/options.json`); a vitest config module's import candidates are unchanged. A `.json` module reached from a vitest config module is locked and not scanned, as today. Type-only imports (`import type ... from './x'`) are imports to the scan, as in item 132. For a Jest config module the *setup keys* are the words `setupFiles`, `setupFilesAfterEnv`, `globalSetup` and `globalTeardown` (with item 132's byte test, or a string whose whole content is one of them), read with item 132's value rule (one literal, or an array of literals). The *root key* is `rootDir`, with item 132's property rule (`:` must follow; `const rootDir = ...` is not one). `setupFiles` and `globalSetup` are setup keys of vitest config modules as today; a vitest config module's `setupFilesAfterEnv` or `rootDir` is nothing to the vitest scan, and a Jest config module's `root` is nothing to the Jest scan.
   - **The root folder.** Jest resolves the paths it reads from its `rootDir`, which is the config's folder unless the config sets it. The *root folder* of a locked Jest config is its own folder, or, when the config itself holds one root key whose value is a literal (followed by `,` or `}`, after comments and whitespace) that does not start with `/`, that literal joined to the config's folder (item 132's join). `import.meta.dirname`, `__dirname`, `'.'` and `'./'` name the config's folder, as item 132 reads them. An empty literal names the config's folder. `<rootDir>` is not replaced in the root key's own value. Anything else is unreadable (point 2, `it sets rootDir`): a value that is not one of those, a literal starting with `/`, a literal that joins above the repository root, a second root key in the same config (the reason is placed at the second key, in text order), and a root key in a module reached by an import (Shipcraft resolves `rootDir` only in the config Jest reads first; write it in the config file itself).
   - **Setup files.** Each literal of a read setup key of a Jest config module names a path, resolved against the root folder of the Jest config through which the module was reached, not against the module's folder (Jest resolves these options from `rootDir`; a module reached from configs with different root folders is read once per root folder, and its reasons are taken from its reads in bytewise order of the root folder: the first reason of the first read that has one). The two runners' discoveries are separate: a module reached from both a vitest and a Jest config is read by each with that runner's keys and folders. A literal whose content starts with `<rootDir>/` has that prefix replaced by `./`, and the literal `<rootDir>` alone by `.`; the content is then joined to the root folder. From there item 132's rule applies unchanged: a literal above the repository root, or with no repository file among its candidates, names nothing (a package such as `jest-extended/all`); the candidates are the path, then the path followed by `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`; every candidate that is a path of `repo.files()` and not a folder is locked; a literal whose content started with `./`, `../` or `<rootDir>` (before the replacement) and has no such candidate is unreadable, as is a literal starting with `/`.
   - **The `jest` key of a manifest.** A watched manifest whose bytes, read with `fs::read`, are UTF-8 and parse as JSON (`serde_json`, which Shipcraft already uses) to an object holding a `jest` key is read; any other manifest (not UTF-8, not JSON, not an object, no `jest` key) names nothing and is not unreadable (npm and Jest refuse an invalid manifest themselves, and point 4 still judges it). The `jest` value must be an object, else the manifest is unreadable (`its jest key is not an object`). Its root folder is the manifest's folder, or its `rootDir` when that is a JSON string that does not start with `/` and does not join above the repository root, joined to the manifest's folder; any other `rootDir` value is unreadable (`it sets rootDir`). Each of its setup keys present must be a JSON string or an array of JSON strings, else unreadable (`<key> is not a string or an array of strings`); each string (JSON escapes decoded) is resolved as a setup literal above, against the manifest's root folder. The *JSON reader* reads an options object (the `jest` object, or a JSON config document): its `rootDir` and its setup keys as above, at its top level; and each entry of its `projects` key that is an object is read as an options object of its own, recursively. A project object's root folder is its parent's root folder, or, when it has a `rootDir` string, that string with a leading `<rootDir>` replaced by the parent's root folder (`<rootDir>/packages/api`), else joined to the parent's root folder (`packages/api`), as Jest resolves an inline project; a project `rootDir` that is not a string, starts with `/` or joins above the repository root is unreadable (`it sets rootDir`). Reasons inside one options object come in this order: its `rootDir`, its setup keys in the order below, then its `projects` objects in array order, depth first. A `projects` entry that is a string (a path or glob of configs) is not followed. A `projects` value that is not an array is ignored, as Jest validates it.
   - **What qualifies.** As in item 132: a candidate for a Jest config, a config module or a setup file that `fs::symlink_metadata` says is a symbolic link makes its config module unreadable; a watched manifest that is a symbolic link is read through the link at `red` (it is not locked), and the hook judges it (point 4). A read error on a config module or a watched manifest, a `fs::symlink_metadata` error on any candidate (a tracked `jest.config.js` deleted from the working tree only, as item 132's `kind` treats it), or `repo.files()` failing, makes `red` fail as `locked_files` fails today (exit 2, no lock written, the old lock kept on a redo); such a failure wins over any unreadable reason found earlier in the discovery. A candidate or a watched manifest that is a folder (a submodule named `package.json`) is skipped. The test files keep today's reading.
   - **The discovery** runs to the end for both runners (every reachable module and every watched manifest read) before point 2 judges, so its result does not depend on traversal order.
   - **The lock.** `files` holds, as today, every test file, `.shipcraft.toml` and item 132's paths, plus the Jest config modules and the setup files point 1 names, each once, hashed with `fs::read` as today. The `RED locked at` and `RED redone at` counts include them. `red --redo` computes the set again from the tree.
2. **When Shipcraft cannot read a Jest config, `red` refuses `setup-unreadable`.** Item 132's refusal, at the same place (where `locked_files` runs, before the lock is written or replaced), naming the first unreadable config module or manifest in bytewise path order among both runners' (when one path is unreadable to both runners, the vitest wording is used). For a Jest config module or manifest the lines are:
   `shipcraft refused: could not read the jest setup files of <config>: <why>`
   `Why: red locks the setup files it can name; one it cannot name could change what every locked case sees`
   `Next: in <config>, write setupFiles, setupFilesAfterEnv, globalSetup and globalTeardown as string literals or arrays of them, and rootDir, if any, as one relative string literal in the config file itself, then run red again`
   `<why>` is, for the first of these the file holds in text order (in a manifest: `jest` first, then `rootDir`, then the setup keys in the order `setupFiles`, `setupFilesAfterEnv`, `globalSetup`, `globalTeardown`, each value's strings in order): item 132's `<key> is not a string or an array of strings`, `<literal> is an absolute path`, `<literal> names no file in the repository`, `<path> is a symbolic link`, `an import is not a string literal`, and the new `it sets rootDir`, `its jest key is not an object` and `it is not a JSON object`. A vitest config module keeps item 132's lines byte for byte. `<config>`, `<literal>` and `<path>` go through `red::one_line`.
3. **Item 132's line names the runner.** The line `red` and `red --redo` print right before `RED locked at` (or `RED redone at`) for the lock's paths that match no suite's globs and are not `.shipcraft.toml` becomes `shipcraft: red also locked what <runners> beside the tests: <list>`, where `<runners>` is `vitest reads` when the config has a vitest suite and no Jest suite, `jest reads` when it has a Jest suite and no vitest suite, and `vitest and jest read` when it has both. Everything else is item 132's point 3 (the list, its order, `and <n> more`, its place after item 98's controls line, none on a refusal or on `RED unchanged`). A config with vitest suites only prints today's line byte for byte.
4. **The hook and CI judge Jest's configs and the `jest` key while a lock is open.** Both checks run for every bound lock whose change is not `Opened` (the hook for the index, CI for each commit), with item 132's and item 138's rules for listing a snapshot's paths and reading its config (`Config::at`, nothing without a config or without a Jest suite).
   - **An added Jest config.** Item 132's `runner-config-added` check (`check_added`) also refuses a path that, in the judged snapshot, would be a locked Jest config of point 1 for a Jest suite of the snapshot's config, that is absent from every parent and not in the lock's `files`. The candidates of both runners are judged together in bytewise path order, the first named. For a Jest config the `Why:` line is `Why: jest reads its settings from this file, so adding one during GREEN can change the judge mid-game`; the first and `Next:` lines are item 132's. A vitest runner config keeps item 132's lines. This refuses (D).
   - **The `jest` key.** Right after item 138's `pytest-config-changed` check, a new check takes the watched manifests of every Jest suite of the snapshot's config among the snapshot's paths and every parent's paths (listed as item 138 lists them), each once, in bytewise order, and refuses with code `jest-config-changed` the first whose *Jest settings* in the snapshot equal those of no parent. A path's Jest settings are *none* when the path is absent from the snapshot; *linked* (equal to nothing, so always refused) when it is a symbolic link there (git mode `120000`); otherwise, read with `Repo::read`, when the bytes are UTF-8 and parse as JSON to an object, the value of its `jest` key compared as a parsed `serde_json::Value` (object key order and whitespace do not count; a duplicate key keeps its last value, as `JSON.parse` does; `1` and `1.0` differ), or *none* when the object has no `jest` key; and when they do not parse as a JSON object, the file's bytes, which never equal a parsed value. The lines:
     `shipcraft refused: jest's settings in <path> <done> <place> with lock <lock> open`
     `Why: Jest reads how the suite runs from the jest key (setup files, module mappings, transforms), so changing it during GREEN changes the judge mid-game`
     `Next: undo the change to the jest key in <path>; if the suite needs it, make it after the cycle closes`
     `<done>`, `<place>`, `<path>` and `<lock>` are item 138's (`are behind a symbolic link`, `were added`, `were removed`, `changed`; `snapshot.describe()`; `red::one_line`), and so are the order, the merge rule (a merge whose settings equal one parent's is accepted), the closing commit (`Closed` judged like any commit that is not `Opened`) and the read failures (exit 2). This refuses (C).
   - Only the `jest` key is judged: a GREEN that changes a manifest's dependencies, scripts or version is accepted, as item 138 accepts a change to `pyproject.toml`'s other tables.

This is the stricter path the threat model asks for, applied the way items 132 and 138 apply it: what Jest names is locked at `red` from the tree, and the manifest, which a GREEN legitimately changes for dependencies, is judged only by its `jest` key, parent by parent, so it needs no migration and judges locks written before this release.

**Existing locks and configs.** No migration, no new lock key, no new format. A lock written before this release keeps its `files`, and the hook and CI judge it by them: a Jest setup file it does not hold stays unjudged until the next `red` or `red --redo`; point 4 applies to it (an added Jest config and a changed `jest` key are refused under an old lock). A lock written by this release is read by older binaries as today, without point 4. `init` writes the same config and globs.

**The version: 2.81.0.** A fix, but not a patch: it adds a refusal code (`jest-config-changed`), `runner-config-added` and `setup-unreadable` now reach Jest suites, and a Jest config whose setup keys are built dynamically is refused at `red` where 2.80.0 locked. Nothing breaks a config, a lock or a command, so it is minor. `init` writes `shipcraft_min = "2.81"`; existing configs keep theirs.

**Known limits.**
- Presets are not read: a relative `preset` (a `jest-preset.js` in the project) and what it names are not locked, and a package preset lives in `node_modules`. Only the four setup keys name files: a file named by `testEnvironment`, `transform`, `moduleNameMapper` (present at RED), `resolver`, `snapshotResolver`, `testSequencer`, `testRunner` or `reporters` is locked only when the globs match it, though changing those keys themselves is refused (`test-changed` on a locked `jest.config.*`, `jest-config-changed` in a manifest).
- `projects` entries that are paths are not followed: a project config under the suite's root is locked by its name, one outside it is not read. Inline project objects are read in JSON (a manifest or a JSON config) and refused in JavaScript when they set `rootDir` (below).
- Options on the command line are not interpreted (`--config`, `-c`, `--rootDir`, `--projects`, `--setupFiles`), as item 138 does not interpret pytest's. A config above the repository root is not read.
- Jest's own module resolution (`moduleDirectories`, `modulePaths`, `index.*` in a folder) is not followed for setup literals; a setup file that imports a helper outside the globs leaves that helper unlocked, as in item 132.
- What transforms the files is not judged: `babel.config.*`, `.babelrc` and the `tsconfig.json` that `ts-jest` reads can change what the tests run while the lock is open, as `tsconfig.json` can for `[build]` (section 9).
- Every watched manifest and Jest config is judged even when Jest would not pick it (a `package.json` `jest` key beside a `jest.config.js`, which Jest refuses as two configs; a nested package's manifest in a monorepo): the deliberate stricter path, counted by the metric. A watched manifest that is a symbolic link is refused on every GREEN commit that holds it while a lock is open, as item 138 refuses a linked `pytest.ini`.
- A `rootDir` built in code (`path.join(__dirname, 'src')`) refuses `setup-unreadable` even with no setup key, and so does a `rootDir` in a shared module the config imports, or two root keys in one JavaScript config (inline `projects` objects that each set `rootDir`): write `rootDir` once, as a relative literal, in the config file, and move inline projects into their own `jest.config.*` files (or into a JSON config, whose `projects` objects are read).
- Type-only imports (`import type { X } from './src/feature'`) are followed, as in item 132, so a TypeScript Jest config that imports product types locks them, and the GREEN gets `test-changed` there; keep the config's imports out of the product.
- A setup literal that names a workspace package (`@acme/test-support/register`, linked in `node_modules` to a tracked `packages/test-support/register.js`) is a package to Shipcraft: the linked file is not locked unless the globs match it. A setup file generated by `[build]` into an ignored folder (`<rootDir>/dist/test-setup.js`) names no file in the repository and refuses `setup-unreadable`; point Jest at the tracked source through a transform instead.
- A suite is a Jest suite by the substring `jest` in its command, as items 132 and 138 find their runners: a wrapper (`npm test`) that runs Jest is not one, and a command that only mentions `jest` (a report folder `jest-results/`) is one, so its Jest configs and manifests are read.
- A redo cannot repair the `jest` key: a redo commit may change only the locks' paths (item 46), and a manifest is not one, so a RED whose `jest` key is wrong is repaired by rewriting the branch's history, as a wrong `pytest.ini` is under item 138. Locked setup files are repaired by a redo as today.
- The checks run only where 2.81.0 runs: a project whose hook or CI uses an older binary is not protected until it upgrades.

**Metric:** on the release, the reproduction's (A) and (B) GREEN commits are refused `test-changed`, (C) `jest-config-changed` and (D) `runner-config-added`, with real Jest. False refusals: GREEN commits refused `jest-config-changed`, or `runner-config-added` or `test-changed` on a path this item added, where the change was not a test shortcut, and `setup-unreadable` refusals of Jest configs, counted from each refusal over the first 10 such refusals in any project we run (POC-051's Node runs included). Revert: above 1 false refusal in those 10, a release narrows points 1 and 4 to the suite's root folder (Jest configs and manifests directly in it, none under it at depth or above it) and lists the rest as known limits.

### The config a vitest suite's command makes vitest read is locked (item 154)

Wrong-verdict note. In v2.0.0 (`nucleo/src/lang.rs`'s Node profile, `git tag --contains 4f9d784`, the oldest tag): nothing locks the config a vitest suite's command names with `--config`, nor a config vitest finds above the suite's root, nor the setup files such a config names. Item 132 (2.75.0) locked the configs it finds by name under the suite's root and resolved their setup files from each config's own folder; it recorded the rest as a known limit (its "Known limits": "a vitest config passed with `--config` or `--root`, or named otherwise ... its setup files are resolved from the config's folder, not from the invocation root, and a config outside a suite's root is not read"), in item 132's spec commit `3dd9c3d` (2026-11-19T11:28:44-03:00). The layer that should have caught it is section 1's guarantee ("its support files, or the config that says how the suite runs"); item 132 closed it only for the configs it finds by name.

**Reproduction, on main (2.90.0, `bc2ba75`):** a scratch repository with real vitest (`vitest@5.0.4`, the battery's version, installed offline from its npm cache) and a hand-written config (`test_command = "node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config config/vitest.unit.ts --reporter=default --reporter=junit --outputFile.junit={junit}"`, 2.0.0's globs), `init --lang node`, one failing case `src/sum.test.ts::adds` against a stub `src/sum.ts` that throws, and `config/vitest.unit.ts` holding `export default {test:{setupFiles:["./src/unit-setup.ts"]}};` (vitest resolves `./src/unit-setup.ts` from its root, the folder it runs in, not from `config/`). `red` locks 2 files (`.shipcraft.toml`, `src/sum.test.ts`). A GREEN commit that changes only `src/unit-setup.ts`, to `import {vi} from "vitest";vi.mock("./sum",()=>({sum:()=>3}));`, passes the hook (`all locked cases pass`) and the lock closes. `src/sum.ts` still throws.

The first RED case reproduces it on main: it fails on 2.90.0 because the hook accepts the commit.

**How vitest picks its config.** The one place that lists every way vitest picks the config a run reads, checked in the sources of vitest 2.1.9, 3.2.4, 4.0.5 and 5.0.4 on 2026-11-22 (`createVitest`/`resolveConfigPath`, `cliOptionsConfig`, `resolveConfig`'s `setupFiles`), and what Shipcraft reads of each:

| Way | What vitest does | This item |
|---|---|---|
| `--config <path>`, `--config=<path>`, `-c <path>`, `-c=<path>` | reads that file; vitest 2.1.9 and 3.2.4 resolve it as a path from vitest's root, 4.0.5 and 5.0.4 first try the value as a module name from the root (a package's config, `@org/test-config`), then the path | read (point 1): always as a path from the root (a module name: a known limit) |
| `--no-config` | reads no config file | read: no named config |
| `--root <path>`, `--root=<path>`, `-r <path>`, `-r=<path>` | vitest's root is that folder, from the folder it runs in; the config is looked up and setup files resolved from it | read (point 1) |
| no `--config` | the first of `vitest.config.<ext>`, then `vite.config.<ext>`, `<ext>` in the order `ts`, `mts`, `cts`, `js`, `mjs`, `cjs`, in the root; vitest 2 to 4 then try each folder above, up to the file system's root; 5.0.4 tries only the root | read: the same order in the root; then, unless the suite's vitest is version 5 or later (point 2), each folder above it up to the repository's root |
| the config's `root` key, and vitest 5's `test.root` | vitest's root becomes that folder (`import.meta.dirname` and `__dirname` name the config module's folder, `'.'` and `'./'` the folder vitest runs in); `--root` wins over it; vitest 5.0.4 takes the top-level root and not `test.root` | item 132's accepted values only; point 2 resolves from vitest's root and, without `--root`, also from each folder an `import.meta.dirname` or `__dirname` root key names, wherever the key is (a deliberate superset) |
| `setupFiles`, `globalSetup` | resolved from vitest's root, not from the config's folder | resolved from the named config's vitest root (point 2) |
| a config above the repository's root | read by vitest 2 to 4 when no config is found inside it | not read (a known limit: it is not in the repository, so no commit the hook judges can change it) |
| `vitest.workspace.<ext>`, `vitest.projects.<ext>`, `--workspace`, the `workspace` and `projects` keys | vitest 2 and 3 only for the first three (removed in vitest 4); project configs a key or file lists | item 132's rule for `vitest.workspace.<ext>` under the root, unchanged; the others stay item 132's known limit |
| a command that reaches vitest through a program that is not a wrapper (`npm test`, `npm run <script>`, `sh -c '...'`), or moves the folder for it (`pnpm -C <dir>`, `pnpm --dir`, `npm --prefix`); a here-document | the script's or program's options and folder decide | not read: a known limit (the options live in `package.json` or in another program's arguments); a wrapper (point 1) whose `vitest` word Shipcraft cannot place is refused, and so is a here-document |
| `cd` or `pushd` before vitest in the command, outside a parenthesized group that closes before vitest | vitest runs in another folder | refused (point 3) |

**A config outside the suite's root is locked, not refused.** A package suite whose folder holds no config runs the repository's root config under vitest 2 to 4 (the monorepo layout item 71 writes for workspaces), and that config is in the repository, so a GREEN could change it in a commit the hook judges; locking it closes that route at no cost to a project that does not change its root config during a lock, while refusing would stop every such suite at `red` with nothing the user could fix but moving the config. Under vitest 5 or later, which does not look above its root, the walk does not either (point 2), so nothing above the root is locked there.

Everything in items 13, 15c, 43, 46, 53, 55, 60, 65, 98, 132, 138, 140 and 141 holds unless a point below changes it: what the hook and CI judge (every path in the lock's `files`, by hash), the existing refusal codes, the lock format, the selection, the controls, the second run, item 132's runner configs and the folder their own setup literals resolve from, item 140's Jest discovery. `red` and `red --redo` hash more paths into `files` for vitest suites, `setup-unreadable` gains a first line and its reasons, and item 132's `runner-config-added` check also judges every named config of every invocation (point 4).

1. **`red` reads the config options of each vitest invocation in a vitest suite's command.** For every vitest suite (item 132's: `command` contains `vitest`), the command as written in the config (`test_command`, or a `[[suite]]`'s `command`, before `{junit}` is replaced) is split into tokens the way `sh` splits it, in this subset:
   - **Tokens.** Unquoted spaces and tabs (U+0020, U+0009; no other character) separate words. An unquoted newline, `;`, `&` and `|` each end the current word and are a *control operator*; an unquoted `(` and `)` end the current word and are an *opening* and a *closing* operator (also control operators). An unquoted `<` or `>` is a *redirection*: it ends the current word, and a word made only of ASCII digits, written with no quote and no backslash, right before it (its file descriptor, `2>`) is dropped (`\2026>x` and `'2026'>x` keep `2026` as a word); the `<`, `>`, `&` and `|` characters right after it belong to it (`>>`, `2>&1`, `>|`); the next word is its operand and is not a word of the command; `<<` (a here-document) makes the whole command unreadable (`it holds a here-document`). `'...'` keeps its content as is. In `"..."`, a backslash before a newline drops both, a backslash before `"`, `\`, `$` or `` ` `` is dropped and keeps the next character, and any other backslash is kept with the character after it. Outside quotes, a backslash before a newline drops both (a line continuation), and before any other character is dropped and keeps that character. Quotes join with what touches them (`--root='my web'` is one word). An unquoted `#` at the start of a word starts a comment that ends right before the next newline (the newline is still an operator). A quote that does not close, or a backslash at the very end, makes the whole command unreadable (`its quotes do not close`). Nothing is expanded: `$`, `` ` ``, `*`, `?`, `[` and `~` stay as written.
   - **Invocations.** A *simple command* is the run of words between two control operators (or the command's start or end). Its *command word* is its first word that is neither a variable assignment (`NAME=value`, `NAME` an ASCII letter or `_` followed by ASCII letters, digits and `_`) nor one of the reserved words `if`, `then`, `else`, `elif`, `do`, `while`, `until`, `!` and `{` (so `if true; then vitest ...; fi` is read). A simple command holds an *invocation* when its command word, after its last `/`, is exactly `vitest` (`vitest`, `node_modules/.bin/vitest`, `../../node_modules/.bin/vitest`), or when its command word is a *wrapper* (exactly `npx`, `bunx`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun`, `npm`, `env`, `exec`, `time`, `nice` or `command`) and the first word after it that does not start with `-`, is not a variable assignment and is not `exec`, `x` or `dlx` is the invocation word or another wrapper, followed the same way (`npx --no -- vitest`, `pnpm exec vitest`, `env CI=1 npx vitest`). A simple command whose command word is a wrapper, that holds no invocation by this rule, but holds a later word whose text after its last `/` is `vitest` (`env -u NODE_OPTIONS vitest`, `nice -n 10 vitest`), is unreadable: `<wrapper> runs vitest in a form Shipcraft does not read` (Shipcraft knows no wrapper's option arity, and refusing is the stricter path). Any other word spelled `vitest` (an argument of `printf`, a test filter) is not an invocation. The invocation's *arguments* are the words after the invocation word in its simple command, and the reading stops early at a word `--` (vitest's end of options). A command can hold several invocations, one per simple command; each is read in command order. A command with none (`npm test`) names no config: the suite keeps item 132's reading only.
   - **Options.** In an invocation's arguments, a word `--config`, `-c`, `--root` or `-r` takes the next argument as its value, unless there is none or it starts with `-`; a word starting with `--config=`, `-c=`, `--root=` or `-r=` carries its value after the first `=`; a word `--no-config` sets no config. Other words are not read and no other option's arity is known, so a value of another option spelled like one of these (`-t --config`) is read as that option, and a grouped short flag such as `-uc` is not split (known limits). Each option is read at most once per invocation (`--config`, `-c` and `--no-config` are one option, `--root` and `-r` the other).
   - **Unreadable.** An invocation is unreadable (besides the wrapper reason above) with the first of these: a `cd` or `pushd` in force (below): `<word> runs before vitest` (`cd` or `pushd`); then, in argument order, `<option> is given more than once` (`<option>` always the long form, `--config` or `--root`, whatever form was written); `<name> has no value` (`<name>` as written: `--config`, `-c`, `--root` or `-r`; also for an empty value, `--config=` or `-c ''`); `<name> <value> is not a plain path` (the value holds `$`, `` ` ``, `*`, `?` or `[`, or starts with `~`); `<name> <value> is an absolute path` (it starts with `/`).
   - **A folder change.** A simple command whose command word is `cd` or `pushd` puts it *in force* at the current parenthesis depth (the number of opening operators read so far minus the closing ones, never below 0); a closing operator that brings the depth below that depth ends it. A `cd` or `pushd` in force when an invocation is read makes it unreadable, even when a later `cd` would return to the suite's folder (`cd tools && make; cd ..; vitest` is refused: a known limit; `(cd tools && make); vitest` is read).
2. **The named config of an invocation is a config module, and its setup files resolve from vitest's root.**
   - **The root.** An invocation's *vitest root* is `--root`'s value joined to the suite's root (item 132's join: `.` and empty segments dropped, each `..` removing the segment before it), or the suite's root without `--root`. A value that joins above the repository root is unreadable: `--root <value> names a folder above the repository root`. With `--root`, each folder of the vitest root from the repository's root down (each prefix of its path) that is not the suite's root or one of its parent folders is checked with `fs::symlink_metadata` in the working tree: the first that is a symbolic link makes the invocation unreadable (`--root <value> goes through a symbolic link`, since `repo.files()` lists a linked folder's files under the link's target, not under the link); a folder that does not exist or cannot be read is not one, and the vitest root stays the lexical join (the walk starts there even when it does not exist).
   - **The named config.** With `--no-config`, none. With `--config`, its value joined to the vitest root, unreadable with the first of: the join is above the repository root (`--config <value> names a file above the repository root`); the path is not in `repo.files()` (`--config <value> names no file in the repository`); its last component's extension is not `ts`, `mts`, `cts`, `js`, `mjs` or `cjs` (`--config <value> is not a .ts, .mts, .cts, .js, .mjs or .cjs file`: Shipcraft can scan only those, and vitest's own lookup uses only those). Without either, the walk: in the vitest root, then in each folder above it up to the repository root, the names `vitest.config.ts`, `vitest.config.mts`, `vitest.config.cts`, `vitest.config.js`, `vitest.config.mjs`, `vitest.config.cjs`, `vite.config.ts`, `vite.config.mts`, `vite.config.cts`, `vite.config.js`, `vite.config.mjs`, `vite.config.cjs`, in that order; the first that is a path of `repo.files()` is the named config; a name that is not one is checked with `fs::symlink_metadata` in the working tree: a regular file or a symbolic link there (a config git ignores, which vitest would read) makes the invocation unreadable (`<path> is a vitest config git does not list`), a folder or `NotFound` is skipped, and any other error fails `red` as a read failure (exit 2, no lock written, the old lock kept on a redo, as item 132's `kind` fails); none found, none named. When the invocation's vitest is *version 5 or later*, `red`'s walk stops after the vitest root. The version is read from one `package.json`: for an invocation word holding a `/` that does not start with `/`, the word joined to the suite's root must end with `node_modules/.bin/vitest`, and the file is `node_modules/vitest/package.json` in that same `node_modules` folder (`../../node_modules/.bin/vitest` in suite `packages/ui` reads `node_modules/vitest/package.json`); any other path word gives no evidence; for a word with no `/` (`vitest`, reached directly or through a wrapper), the first `node_modules/vitest/package.json` that `fs::read` reads, looking in the suite's root folder, then in each folder above it up to the repository's root. Its bytes are parsed as JSON (`serde_json`) and its `version` string read: when that string starts with an ASCII digit, its leading run of ASCII digits, leading zeros dropped, is 5 or more when it has two or more digits left or is the digit 5 to 9 (`"5.0.4"`, `"5"`, `"10.1.0"`); no file read, a file that is not JSON, no `version` string, or one that does not start with a digit, give no evidence, and the walk goes up (vitest 2 to 4's rule, the stricter one: under vitest 5 it can lock a config above the root that vitest does not read, a known limit). In this point `<value>` is the value as written and the option is named in its long form.
   - **What is locked.** Each named config is a *config module* of item 132's point 1, exactly as a locked runner config is: scanned, its relative imports followed to any depth and resolved from the importing module's own folder, its symbolic-link and read-failure rules, its unreadable reasons (item 132's point 2: a variable setup value, an absolute literal, a relative literal or import with no candidate, a link, a built import, a root key other than the four accepted values). A path that is both a locked runner config and a named config is one config module.
   - **Where its setup literals resolve.** A named config's *root folders* are its vitest root and, without `--root`, the folder of every module reached from that named config (the named config itself or a module it imports) that holds a root key `import.meta.dirname` or `__dirname`, wherever the key stands (top level or inside `test`). This is a deliberate superset of what vitest reads (its root is one of these folders; Shipcraft does not order vite's merge, nor tell a top-level `root` from vitest 5's ignored `test.root`): it can lock a file vitest does not read beside the one it does, never miss the one it does. To report such a key, the scan gives an event for an accepted vitest root key `import.meta.dirname` or `__dirname` (not for `'.'` or `'./'`, which name the folder vitest runs in, already the vitest root without `--root`); item 132's and item 140's readings are otherwise unchanged. The root folders of a named config are found from its whole graph before any setup literal is resolved, so a literal written before the root key resolves from them too, and a module reached from several named configs resolves its literals from each one's root folders (the paths found are united). A setup literal of a module reached from a named config names, with item 132's candidates (the path, then the path with each of its eight extensions; every candidate that is a file of `repo.files()` locked), the paths it gives from each of its root folders. A module reached also from item 132's runner configs keeps its own folder too, as today (item 132's behavior, kept for compatibility, which can also lock a file vitest does not read). A literal that joins above the repository root from a folder gives nothing from that folder; one that joins above it from every folder of the module names nothing and is not unreadable (item 132's rule for `../outside.ts`). A relative literal that joins inside the repository from at least one folder is unreadable (`<literal> names no file in the repository`) when no folder gives a candidate. Within one literal the folders are tried in bytewise order and each folder's candidates in item 132's order; a symbolic-link candidate gives item 132's link reason even when another folder gives a file; the module's reason is the first in text order, as in item 132.
   - **The lock.** `files` holds, as today, every test file, `.shipcraft.toml`, item 132's and item 140's paths, plus the named configs, the modules they reach and the setup files they name, each once, hashed with `fs::read`. The `RED locked at` and `RED redone at` counts include them, and item 132's point 3 line names those that match no suite's globs, with item 140's runner wording kept as it is (`vitest reads`, `jest reads` or `vitest and jest read`, chosen from the config's suites, so a vitest-only config prints `shipcraft: red also locked what vitest reads beside the tests: <list>`). `red --redo` computes the set again from the tree.
3. **When Shipcraft cannot read the command, `red` refuses `setup-unreadable`.** Where `locked_files` runs (after the first run, so the run's outputs, temporaries and row are as today), before the lock is written or replaced, after `repo.files()` is listed (a listing failure fails `red` first, exit 2, as today) and before any config module is read: the suites in config order, and in each, a whole-command reason (`its quotes do not close`, `it holds a here-document`) first, then its simple commands in command order, each judged by point 1's order (a wrapper's reason, or an invocation's `cd`/`pushd` reason and then its options' reasons), then point 2's root, link and `--config` reasons and the walk's, the first unreadable one refuses:
   `shipcraft refused: could not read the vitest config of <key>: <why>`
   `Why: red locks the config vitest reads and the setup files it names; a config it cannot name could change what every locked case sees`
   `Next: in .shipcraft.toml, give vitest's --config and --root at most once each, as plain relative paths, with no cd before vitest, then run red again`
   `<key>` is `test_command` for a config with no `[[suite]]`, else `command of [[suite]] <name>` (`<name>` the suite's `name`, or its root as messages show it, through `red::one_line`), as item 134 names a suite's command. `<why>` is one of point 1's and point 2's reasons; every `<value>` in it goes through `red::one_line`. An unreadable named config module (a link, a variable setup value) refuses with item 132's lines, naming the module, in item 132's bytewise order among item 132's and item 140's unreadable modules.
4. **The hook and CI refuse a config added where vitest would now read it.** Item 132's `runner-config-added` check (`vitest_files::check_added`, for every bound lock whose change is not `Opened`, wherever it runs: the hook, `ci`, and item 141's post-commit check of an unjudged commit through `ci::check_commit`) also takes, for each vitest suite of the judged snapshot's config, the named config of every invocation point 1 reads without a reason, found among the snapshot's paths (the walk, or `--config`'s path, over the snapshot's path list as item 132 lists it). Only point 1's reasons and point 2's lexical ones (`--root` or `--config` above the repository root, `--config` naming no path of the snapshot or a non-JavaScript one) apply there: a whole command that is unreadable adds nothing, an unreadable invocation adds nothing while the others still add theirs, and in the snapshot the walk reads no file, checks no link, never refuses and always goes up to the repository root whatever the vitest version, so the verdict on a commit does not depend on the installed dependencies or the working tree). Every such path, absent from every parent and not in the lock's `files`, is refused with item 132's three lines (`runner config <path> was added <place> with lock <lock> open`, its `vitest` `Why:` and its `Next:`), all the snapshot's named configs, item 132's and item 140's candidates taken together, once each, in bytewise order, the first named. This refuses a GREEN that adds `web/vitest.config.ts` to a suite rooted in `web` whose lock holds the root's `vitest.config.ts`, and one that adds `vitest.config.ts` beside a locked `vite.config.ts` above the suite's root.

**Existing locks and configs.** No migration, no new lock key, no new format. A lock written before this release keeps its `files`, and the hook and CI judge it by them: a named config and its setup files it does not hold stay unjudged until the next `red` or `red --redo`; point 4 applies to it. A lock written by this release is read by older binaries as today, without point 4's new paths. `init` writes the same config and globs.

**The version: 2.92.0.** A fix, but not a patch: `red` locks more paths and refuses a command it cannot read where 2.91.0 locked. Nothing breaks a config, a lock, a command or a refusal code, so it is minor. `init` writes `shipcraft_min = "2.91"`; existing configs keep theirs. If another item takes 2.91.0 first, this item takes the next minor and every version this section names moves with it.

**Known limits.** The table's "not read" rows: a config above the repository's root; a command that reaches vitest through a script or a program that is not a wrapper, or moves its folder other than by `cd` or `pushd` (`pnpm -C`, `npm --prefix`); workspace and projects files and keys beyond item 132's rule. A `--config` value meant as a module name (vitest 4.0.5 and later resolve `--config @org/test-config` as a package first) is read as a path: one naming no file in the repository is refused, and one that also names a repository file (a workspace package `config` exporting `./unit.ts` while `config/unit.ts` exists) locks the repository file, not the package's. Point 1's option reading knows no other option's arity (`-t --config` is read as `--config`) and splits no grouped short flag (`-uc`); a `cd` that later returns (`cd x && make; cd ..; vitest`) is refused, and so is a wrapper whose own options take values (`env -u NODE_OPTIONS vitest`); write such commands with `--root`, a parenthesized group, `=` forms, or the vitest word first. The version rule reads one `package.json` chosen by the invocation word's path; a vitest found elsewhere by Node's resolution (a `NODE_PATH`, a global install, a package manager's store with no `node_modules/vitest` folder) gives no evidence, and the walk then goes up, which under vitest 5 can lock, and refuse a dynamic setup value in, a config above the root that vitest does not read (the deliberate stricter path; point 4 always goes up for the same reason). Point 2's root folders are a superset of vitest's root (an `import.meta.dirname` root key in an imported module that the config never merges, a `test.root` vitest 5 ignores, and item 132's own-folder rule kept for modules its runner configs reach), so a file vitest does not read can be locked beside the one it does. A named config that imports product code locks it, as in item 132. A path that is both a named vitest config and a Jest config name (`vitest run -c jest.config.mjs`, whose command also makes the suite a Jest suite) and is added while a lock is open is refused `runner-config-added` as point 4 says, but with item 140's Jest `Why:` line (`Why: jest reads its settings from this file, ...`) instead of the vitest one: the verdict is right, only the runner word is wrong (review round 2, recorded as a known limit).
