### `red`, `status` and `report` stop printing three false lines (item 136)

Wrong-verdict note. Three lines say something the run did not observe, each since a different release; one `--fixes-release` must cover all three, so it names the oldest (`git tag --contains <commit>`, the oldest tag of each):
- `status`'s branch protection line, since v2.0.0 (`nucleo/src/merge.rs`, commit `4f9d784`): any `gh api` error holding `404` prints `<base> has no branch protection`, and any holding `403` prints `this repository has no branch protection (GitHub free plan)`. GitHub answers `404 Not Found` (not `404 Branch not protected`) when the account is not an admin of the repository, so the line asserts an absence it never saw.
- `report`'s lock state, since v2.1.0 (item 38, commit `7afed8c`): `open` for every lock without a passed `merge` row, also when its close was observed.
- `report`'s DORA `per day`, since v2.34.0 (item 76, commit `88b79f8`): count ÷ span for any span above zero, so two merges minutes apart print thousands per day.
- `red`'s controls line, since v2.48.0 (item 98, commit `f620797`): one passing case anywhere in a suite that the mapper ties to no file or to two makes the whole suite's controls empty, so a full run prints `controls: 0` while cases of the changed test files pass.

Found on 2026-11-18 by POC-051 runs 3 (cli/cli: `controls: 0` while 29 cases of the changed files pass; `trunk has no branch protection` as a non-admin), 4 (httpx: the protection line), 5 (expense-compass: the protection line) and 6 (barbearia: `report` printed `lock ...: open; red at ..., close at ...` while `status` said no open lock, and `per day 4430.77` from two direct commits on main), recorded in the POC-051 card (`poc/051-simulated-adopters/FICHA.md`, item 7, commit `18ba6ee`, 2026-11-18T16:20-03:00). The layers that should have caught them: item 5's `status` cases, whose `gh` stub answers only `403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro` or `404 Branch not protected`, never a non-admin's `404 Not Found`; item 38's `v1-38.open` case, which pins `open` for a lock with a close row; item 76's and item 124's DORA cases, which pin a per-day rate over spans of 100 and 200 seconds; item 98's cases, which ran the controls only on fixtures where every passing case maps (and `v1-98.unmapped`, which pins the empty result as intended). A line that states what was not observed is a defect, so this is a fix (`kind = fix`, `red --fix --reported-at 2026-11-18T16:20-03:00 --fixes-release v2.0.0`; v2.0.0 is the oldest of the four releases above). Victor's decision (2026-11-18, "Pode resolver, tá?").

**Reproduction, on main (2.77.0, the shared binary):**
- (A) A copy of the POC-051 cli/cli clone (Go, gotestsum) with the RED's four files uncommitted and a base whose `.shipcraft.toml` differs from the branch's by one value, so `red` runs every suite: `red ran every suite: config changed`, then `controls: 0 passing case(s) of the changed test files`. The same files with the base config unchanged (the narrowed run): `controls: 29 ...`. The full run's 9,814 passing cases include `TestNormalizeReference` and its 8 subtests, defined in both `artifact_posix_test.go` (`//go:build !windows`) and `artifact_windows_test.go` (`//go:build windows`) of one package, which the Go mapper ties to two files.
- (B) A repository whose origin is any GitHub repository, `status` with a `gh` on `PATH` that answers the protection call with exit 1, stdout `{"message":"Not Found",...,"status":"404"}` and stderr `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)` (what `gh api repos/cli/cli/branches/trunk/protection` answers a non-admin): `main has no branch protection: \`shipcraft merge\` is the gate`. A repository whose branch truly has no protection answers `{"message":"Branch not protected",...}` and `gh: Branch not protected (HTTP 404)`.
- (C) A local repository with no remote: two direct commits on `main` 5 seconds apart, `init`, a branch, a RED commit and a GREEN commit whose hook closes the lock. `status`: `open locks: none`. `report`: `lock <id>: open; red at ..., close at ...` and `deploys: 2 merge(s), first at ..., last at ..., per day 34560.00`.

The first RED case reproduces (B) on main: it fails on 2.77.0 because `status` prints `has no branch protection` for a `404 Not Found`.

Everything in items 5, 38, 76, 83, 98, 124 and 125 holds unless a point below changes it.

1. **`red`'s controls are held case by case, and the line says how many passing cases could not be held.** Wherever `red` or `red --redo` computes controls today (not with `--all`, not without a readable base, not on a redo's kept-controls path; item 98), a passing case of a suite is a control when the suite's mapper finds a map and that map ties the case to exactly one file, which is a changed path. The map is inferred exactly as today, once per suite from all of that suite's passing cases (item 81's `coverage_map`, its root and prefix choice, and the Go reader `go_tests`, which reads an unreadable or non-UTF-8 file as declaring no test, all unchanged); only the lookup that follows (`holder` per case) stops being all-or-nothing. An unknown pytest, vitest or jest case that prevents the inference still leaves its suite without a map, so the suite has no controls and all its passing cases count in `m`. A case the map ties to no file or to more than one (a Go test defined in two build-tagged files) is not a control, and no longer empties its suite's controls: the suite's other passing cases are judged one by one. A suite for which the mapper finds no map has no controls, as today. Let `m` be the passing cases of the suites judged that are not controls because of either of those two reasons (no map for the suite, or no single file for the case; cases held to one file that is not a changed path do not count). The controls line (printed where it is today: before item 132's optional vitest notice, which stays immediately before `RED locked at` / `RED redone at`) stays `shipcraft: controls: <n> passing case(s) of the changed test files; the hook runs them too` when `m` is 0, and becomes `shipcraft: controls: <n> passing case(s) of the changed test files; the hook runs them too; <m> passing case(s) could not be tied to a single test file, so they are not controls` when `m` is above 0. Same stream (stdout), same place. The lock's format, its `controls` list (byte order, as today) and the hook's use of it are unchanged; only which cases enter the list changes. With `--all`, without a readable base, and on the kept-controls path, the line is today's, with no `m` clause. `m` is shown only where today's line is printed (a successful write of a format 5 or 6 lock): a redo that writes format 3 (`v1-98.legacy-judge`), a refusal, an unchanged redo and a write failure print no controls line, as today.
2. **`status` says it could not read the protection when GitHub's answer does not prove there is none.** The protection call and its success path are unchanged. For a failed call, with `<e>` the error text as today (`gh`'s stderr, then its stdout, trimmed):
   - `<e>` contains `Upgrade to GitHub Pro`: today's `shipcraft: this repository has no branch protection (GitHub free plan): \`shipcraft merge\` is the gate`;
   - else `<e>` contains `Branch not protected`: today's `shipcraft: <base> has no branch protection: \`shipcraft merge\` is the gate`;
   - else `<e>` contains `HTTP 404`: `shipcraft: could not read branch protection on <base> (GitHub answers 404 when this account is not an admin of the repository, so protection may exist): use \`shipcraft merge\` as the gate`;
   - else (a `403` without the upgrade text, no remote, `gh` missing, any other failure): today's `shipcraft: could not read branch protection (<first line of <e>>): use \`shipcraft merge\` as the gate`.
   Matches are case-sensitive substrings of the whole `<e>`. Exactly one protection line, exit 0, no row, as today. `init --github`'s protection write (item 5.3) follows the same reading: only an error containing `Upgrade to GitHub Pro` prints `this repository has no branch protection on its GitHub plan: \`shipcraft merge\` is the gate.`; any other failure, a `403` included, prints today's `could not mark statuses as required (<e>); \`shipcraft merge\` is the gate.`
3. **`report`'s lock state and per-day rate say what was observed.**
   - **State.** A lock row's `state` is `merged` when it has a qualifying merge (as today: `flow::merge_row`, a passed `merge` row whose `base` equals its `default_branch`, with a readable time); else `merge_not_observed` when its lock file is at the default branch's tip (item 76, as today); else `closed` when its close was observed (`close_at` is not `null`, read as today: the earliest passed non-redo `close` row with a readable time, `passed("close")`); else `open`. The text prints the same word in the same place (`lock <id>: closed; red at ...`). `closed` locks are not counted in day rows (only `merged`, as today) and are not selected by `--github` (only `merged` and `merge_not_observed`, as today). This replaces item 38's reading "`state` (`open` or `merged`)" and item 76's "else `open`".
   - **Per day.** DORA's `deploys.value.per_day` is `null` when the time from the first to the last deploy read is under one day (86,400 seconds), as it is today with fewer than 2 deploys or a zero span; from exactly 86,400 seconds on it is today's count ÷ (span / 86,400). `count`, `first`, `last`, `n`, `missing` and `reason` are unchanged, in release and merge modes alike. The text prints `per day -` for a `null` rate as today, and, when the rate is `null` only because the span is above zero and under a day, `per day - (first to last under a day)` in its place: `deploys: 2 merge(s), first at <time>, last at <time>, per day - (first to last under a day) (n 2, missing 0)`.
   - Times stay UTC (item 83); the local offset is a later item.

**The version: 2.78.1.** A patch: three outputs now say what was observed. No command, flag, config key, lock format or refusal code changes. `report --json`'s `state` gains the value `closed` for a lock that printed `open` with a close time, and `per_day` is `null` in more cases; a reader that handles `null` and an unknown state word keeps working. Item 135 took 2.78.0 first, so this item is 2.78.1.

### `report --github`'s code split into modules (item 119)

This item changes Shipcraft's own code, not the product: no command, config key, lock, refusal, row, `gh` call or output of `shipcraft` changes. `nucleo/src/relatorio_gh.rs`, the code that asks GitHub through `gh` for `report --github` (items 79, 113 and 114), has 716 lines on `origin/main` `ec1880f` (525 of code and 191 of unit tests); since items 116 and 117 it is one of the larger files in `nucleo/src`, and items 113 and 114 each grew it. This item moves its code, unchanged, into modules along its own seams, by item 116's method. It is a refactor: a patch release, 2.63.4 (item 118, running beside it, takes 2.63.3; whichever of the two merges second rebases onto the other).

1. **The modules.** `nucleo/src/relatorio_gh.rs` stays the module root (Rust's `relatorio_gh.rs` beside a `relatorio_gh/` folder) and its submodules go in `nucleo/src/relatorio_gh/`, exactly these files, each holding the items named, defined nowhere else:

   | File | What it holds | Items (each defined in this file only) |
   |---|---|---|
   | `relatorio_gh.rs` | the module root: the reasons every reader gives, the PR a lock went through and a call's outcome; it declares the six submodules | `const FAILED`, `const UNREADABLE`, `const TIMED_OUT`, `enum Pr`, `type Outcome` |
   | `relatorio_gh/asker.rs` | the asker: one lock's waiting and merge time (item 79), a commit's Blocking count (item 113), a PR's check runs (item 114), the once-per-run config reader and the call cache with its timeout | `struct Asker` (with its one `impl` block, every method in it unchanged) |
   | `relatorio_gh/answers.rs` | the shapes of `gh`'s answers that several readers share (item 79) | `struct PrView` (with its `impl`), `fn pages`, `fn check_run`, `fn oid`, `fn time` |
   | `relatorio_gh/checks.rs` | item 114's reading of a PR's commits and check runs | `type Tally`, `enum Verdict`, `struct Run`, `fn pr_commits`, `fn suite_runs`, `fn tally` |
   | `relatorio_gh/blocking.rs` | item 113's reading of the review statuses | `fn latest_count`, `fn blocking_count` |
   | `relatorio_gh/process.rs` | running `gh` in its own process group under the 60 s limit | `const LIMIT`, `enum Ran`, `fn run` |
   | `relatorio_gh/tests.rs` | the unit tests, as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` in `relatorio_gh.rs` | the 7 `#[test]` functions of today's `mod tests`: `pr_commits_are_distinct_shas_in_answer_order`, `suite_runs_read_completed_runs_of_the_names`, `each_red_run_is_green_again_fixed_by_a_new_commit_or_still_red`, `a_pr_is_read_in_full_or_gives_its_one_reason`, `blocking_counts_follow_the_grammar`, `the_latest_count_wins_ties_to_the_first`, `times_are_github_utc_real_dates` |

   - **The folder** `nucleo/src/relatorio_gh/` holds exactly the six files named, and nothing else: no other file of any name or extension, no subfolder. `nucleo/src/relatorio.rs` and `nucleo/src/relatorio/` (item 116) are not touched; in particular `relatorio/github.rs`, what `report` asks through the `Asker`, stays where it is.
   - **The submodules are declared** in `relatorio_gh.rs`, each on its own line at column 0: `mod <name>;` for the five code modules (`asker`, `answers`, `checks`, `blocking`, `process`; a `pub(crate) ` or `pub(super) ` prefix allowed), and `mod tests;` on the line right after a line `#[cfg(test)]`.
   - **A definition** is read line by line, with no Rust parser, by item 117's reader: a line at column 0 of the form `[pub ][pub(crate) |pub(super) ][unsafe ](fn|struct|enum|const|type) <name>` followed by a character that cannot continue a Rust identifier (`(`, `<`, `:`, ` `, `;`, `{`, `=`), or `impl <name>` followed by ` ` or `{`. `impl<'a> Asker<'a> {` and `impl<'v> PrView<'v> {` define nothing in this sense (the struct line does). Methods, nested functions and test helpers inside a block are indented, so they are not definitions, and neither are `use` lines (a `pub use` or `pub(crate) use` re-export defines nothing). A test is a line at column 4 or less of the form `fn <name>(` (any leading spaces) whose previous non-blank line is `#[test]` at the same indent.

No other column-0 line starting with `impl` that names `Asker<` or `PrView<` exists in the six code files.

### The config's code split into modules (item 118)

This item changes Shipcraft's own code, not the product: no command, config key, default, lock, refusal, row, file written or output of `shipcraft` changes. `nucleo/src/config.rs`, the code that reads and validates `.shipcraft.toml`, has 1,247 lines on `origin/main` `ec1880f` (978 of code and 269 of unit tests); since item 117 it is the largest file in `nucleo/src`. A file that size is slow to read and to review, and every new config key lands in it. This item moves its code, unchanged, into modules along the config's own seams, by the method of items 116 and 117. It is a refactor: a patch release, 2.63.3.

   - **The trait impls go with their type:** `impl Default for Execucao` in `execution.rs`, `impl Default for Papeis` in `roles.rs`, `impl Default for Revisao` in `review.rs`, `impl Default for Pr`, `impl Default for DependencyDays` and `impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for DependencyDays` in `pr.rs`. They are not table items (the reader below reads `impl Default for X` as an `impl` of `Default`, a name in no row, and `impl<'de>` as no definition), so the cases do not pin them; the move keeps them beside their type. `fn dot` and `fn any_value` stay in the module of the struct whose serde attributes name them (`#[serde(default = "dot")]`, `deserialize_with = "any_value"`), because serde resolves those paths from that module.
   - **The folder** `nucleo/src/config/` holds exactly the ten files named, and nothing else: no other file of any name or extension, no subfolder.
   - **The submodules are declared** in `config.rs`, each on its own line at column 0: `mod <name>;` for the nine code modules (a `pub(crate) ` or `pub(super) ` prefix allowed), and `mod tests;` on the line right after a line `#[cfg(test)]`.
   - **A definition** is read line by line, with no Rust parser, by item 117's reader: a line at column 0 of the form `[pub ][pub(crate) |pub(super) ][unsafe ](fn|struct|enum|const|type) <name>` followed by a character that cannot continue a Rust identifier (`(`, `<`, `:`, ` `, `;`, `{`, `=`), or `impl <name>` followed by ` ` or `{`. Methods, nested functions and struct fields are indented, so they are not definitions in this sense, and neither are `use` lines (a `pub use` or `pub(crate) use` re-export defines nothing) nor `#[...]` attribute lines. A test is a line at column 4 or less of the form `fn <name>(` (any leading spaces) whose previous non-blank line is `#[test]` at the same indent. In `tests.rs` the test helper `fn suite(` sits at column 0 and so counts as a definition of `suite`, a name in no row (the table's `Suite` differs in case). A column-0 definition inside a block comment or a string would be counted; the moved code has none.
   - **Every item keeps its name,** and each table item, the tests included, is defined in exactly one of the eleven files, the one its row names. Uniqueness is by name, whatever the kind, as item 117's: a table item's name defined at column 0 (or as a test) in a file other than its row's fails, even as another kind (`struct Camada` in one file and `enum Camada` in another). A type and its `impl` (`struct Config` and `impl Config`) share their row's file.
   - **A file is at most 600 lines,** counted as the number of `\n` bytes plus one when the file is non-empty and does not end in `\n`. This applies to `config.rs` and to each file in the folder; today's sizes put every file well under (the largest, `tests.rs`, about 270).
   - **Reading fails closed:** a file or the folder that is missing, unreadable, not UTF-8, or not listable fails the case with its path, never passes it.
2. **The code moves unchanged.** Each item's body, attributes (the `#[derive(...)]` and `#[serde(...)]` lines, field by field) and doc comments move as they are, every refusal text and default value byte for byte. Today's two-line `//!` header stays at the head of `config.rs`. The only edits are the ones the move needs: `mod` declarations and `use` lines; visibility widened to `pub(super)` or `pub(crate)` where another module of `config` now uses the item or its struct fields (for example `PapeisRaw`, a private field of `Config`; `Execucao`'s `suite_checks_raw` and `Revisao`'s `after_raw`, which `Config::parse_before_guide` reads; the `check_*`, `normal_path`, `normal_globs`, `not_toml` and `camada` functions `config.rs` calls); one `//!` line at the head of each new file saying what it holds; the unit tests' indentation, one level less outside the `mod tests { }` block, with their names and bodies kept and only their `use` lines changing; and the formatting `cargo fmt` gives. ### `pr --merge` merges when the PR is ready (item 110)

POC-031 (private process repository, `poc/031-pr-then-merge`, 2026-11-07) chained `shipcraft pr` and `shipcraft merge <n>` in a script for Shipcraft's own items: over PRs 116 to 120 the `merge` row came 5 to 7 s after the `pr` row (median 6 s, against 12 to 42 s by hand), and no merge went through that the gate would refuse. Where the chain was not used, the merge waited for whoever came back: PR 124 waited 15 min and PR 126 24 min after `pr` passed. Now `pr` takes the chain itself. The gate does not move: the merge is `shipcraft merge`'s, with the same checks, refusals, pin and row.

1. **The flag.** `shipcraft pr` accepts `--merge`, a flag with no value, in any option position among `--title <t>` and `--body <file>` (`pr --merge`, `pr --title T --merge --body f`, `pr --body f --merge`). The arguments are read left to right as today: `--title` and `--body` each take the next argument as their value whatever it is, so `pr --title --merge` is a PR titled `--merge` without the flag, and `pr --body --merge` reads a file named `--merge`; only a `--merge` in an option position sets the flag. `--title` or `--body` with no argument after it, `--merge` given twice in option positions, a value after it that is not one of the options (`pr --merge yes`), or any other unknown argument is the invalid-arguments error it is today (`shipcraft: error: invalid arguments: ...; usage: ...` on stderr, exit 2), before anything runs: no fetch, no push, no `gh` call, no row. The usage text names it: the `pr` entry becomes `shipcraft pr [--title <t>] [--body <file>] [--merge]`; nothing else in the usage text changes. Without `--merge`, `pr` behaves exactly as today, byte for byte, in its output, exit codes, GitHub calls and rows.
2. **When it merges.** With `--merge`, `pr` runs as today up to and including its last line: ``shipcraft: PR #<n> ready: enabled layers passed; merge with `shipcraft merge <n>`.`` is printed unchanged, and the `pr` row is written as today (same fields, `result` `"passed"`, its `secs` not counting the merge), best effort: a failed append changes neither the merge attempt nor the exit code. Only then, and only when `pr` would have exited 0, it attempts the merge of that PR exactly as `shipcraft merge <n>` without `--no-review` does, in the same process, where `<n>` is the PR number `pr` just printed: the `gh pr view` and its permissive reading as today (a missing or wrong-typed field reads as empty, the number as 0; no new schema check), the fetch of the base, the base's config, the status reads, the suite checks of item 62, the refusals `pr-not-open`, `merge-without-ci` and `merge-without-review`, the `--match-head-commit` pin to the `headRefOid` the merge's own gate reads, `[execution] merge` (`"merge"` or `"squash"`, item 42), the `merge` row, and its two success lines (`shipcraft: PR #<n> merged into <base>.` and item 85's cleanup line), printed on stdout right after the `ready` line. The output after the `ready` line and the exit code are exactly the merge's: 0 when merged; 1 with the merge's refusal on stderr; 2 with `shipcraft: error: ...` where `shipcraft merge` errors (its `gh pr view`, the base fetch, the status read, `gh pr merge`). Item 62's suite-check reads keep their meaning: an unreadable check is the `merge-without-ci` refusal, exit 1, not an error. The gate is read afresh: a base whose config changed while `pr` ran (a new suite check, a layer turned on) may refuse though every layer of this `pr` passed. The `pr` row already written stays `"passed"` whatever the merge does.
3. **When it does not merge.** When `pr` refuses (any code: `pr-not-on-branch`, a CI or review refusal, ...) or errors, `--merge` changes nothing: the same output, exit code and rows as without it, no merge attempted, no `merge` row, no further `gh` call. `--merge` never waives a layer: an off layer passes exactly as `shipcraft merge` already lets it, and there is no `--no-review` for `pr`.

**Known limits.** With `[execution] ci = "github"` and review off, `pr` does not wait for GitHub's CI (items 62 and 73), so the merge that follows usually finds `shipcraft/ci` not yet `success` and refuses `merge-without-ci`; the PR stays open and `shipcraft merge <n>` merges it later. When the merge refuses or errors after `pr` passed, Shipcraft makes no merge and undoes nothing `pr` did (push, PR body, statuses, comment, `pr` row); the PR's state on GitHub is whatever it is (someone else may have closed or merged it, which is `pr-not-open`). The merge reads the PR's head again from GitHub and pins that head, as `shipcraft merge` does: a push that lands after that read is refused by the pin, but a newer head pushed before it, by another session, is merged when it carries every required status at `success`, exactly as a standalone `shipcraft merge` would merge it; `--merge` does not insist on the head this `pr` reviewed. The AGENTS.md block and the briefs do not mention the flag (no block change in this item); the `ready` line still names `shipcraft merge <n>`, which stays valid.

**Metric:** over the next 5 items of our own flow run with `pr --merge` in place of `process/pr-merge.sh`: the gap from the `pr` row to the `merge` row (their `at`), median ≤ 10 s, and 0 merges the gate would refuse (a merge whose head lacks a required status at `success`). Revert: a release that drops the flag; nothing is written by this item that a later binary must read, and the process goes back to `process/pr-merge.sh`.

### `pr` checks origin before it pushes, and `pr` and `merge` refuse with no origin (item 130)

Found on 2026-11-18 by POC-051 (simulated adopters, `poc/051-simulated-adopters/FICHA.md`, queue item 3, seen in all six repositories). Run 5 (a vibe-coded app cloned from its author's public repository): `shipcraft pr` pushed first, to `origin` as it was, with no check that the user can write there, and stopped on git's raw error. Run 6 (a local-only repository, no remote): `pr` stopped on `git fetch -q origin`'s raw error and `merge 1` on `gh pr view`'s `no git remotes found`, with no Why and no Next, and nothing said that the work is local and `shipcraft ci` is its finish line. Run 4 (a contributor clone of `encode/httpx`): origin was the real upstream, and only the run's own stop rule kept `pr` from pushing there. This is a new guard, not a fix: no earlier contract said `pr` checks origin (`kind = feature`).

**Reproduction, on main (2.70.0):**
- No remote: a scratch repository with a commit on `main` and a branch `feat` with one more, no remote. `shipcraft pr --title t` prints ``shipcraft: error: `git fetch -q origin` failed: fatal: 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository`` (and git's three further lines) and exits 2; `shipcraft merge 1` prints ``shipcraft: error: `gh pr view 1 --json number,state,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName` failed: no git remotes found`` and exits 2.
- Origin not writable: the same shape with `shipcraft init` committed on `main`, `origin` = `https://github.com/encode/httpx.git` (for which `gh repo view https://github.com/encode/httpx.git --json viewerPermission` answers `READ`), and `remote.origin.pushurl` set to a local bare repository of the test. `shipcraft pr --title t` prints `shipcraft: feat published to origin (<sha>)`: the branch reached the push URL with no check, and only then did `pr` stop (exit 2).

**Refuse or warn when the permission cannot be proven: refuse, settled here.** The threat is a branch pushed into a repository that is not the user's (someone else's project, or a real upstream). When `gh` cannot answer (not installed, not logged in, offline, origin not on a GitHub host), `pr` cannot tell a writable origin from a foreign one. A warning would push anyway, which is the harm this item exists to stop. And refusing loses nothing that works today: every step of `pr` after the push needs `gh` (`gh pr list`, `gh pr create`, the statuses), so a `pr` whose `gh` cannot read origin's permission already fails today, only after it has pushed. So `pr` refuses, before any fetch, push or `gh` write.

Everything in items 3, 5, 100, 103 and 110 holds unless a point below changes it: the other refusals and their order, exit codes, stdout and stderr of a `pr` or `merge` that passes the check, statuses, comments, rows and files written.

1. **No origin.** "No origin" means `git remote get-url --push --all origin`, run in the repository root, exits with code 2 (git's `error: No such remote 'origin'`). Any other nonzero exit, a git that cannot be started or that ends on a signal, is a failure of shipcraft as `Repo::run` reports it today (`shipcraft: error: ...`, exit 2), never `no-origin`. `<base>` in this point is `main` when `git rev-parse -q --verify refs/heads/main^{commit}` succeeds, else `master` when the same check on `refs/heads/master` succeeds, else the literal text `<base branch>` (so the `Next:` line reads ``shipcraft ci --base <base branch>``); a failure of those checks counts as the ref not existing.
   - Argument parsing and finding the repository keep their precedence: an invalid `pr` or `merge` command line and a directory outside git are refused or fail as today, before this check.
   - `pr` (with or without `--merge`, `--title`, `--body`) checks this first, before any other git call that reaches a remote, before reading the config, before reading the `--body` file and before the `pr-not-on-branch` refusal, so a repository without origin refuses this way even on its default branch or on a detached HEAD. It refuses `no-origin`:
     `shipcraft refused: this repository has no remote named origin, so shipcraft pr has nowhere to open a PR`
     `Why: pr pushes the branch to origin and opens the PR on GitHub; nothing was fetched, pushed or sent`
     ``Next: the work stays local, and `shipcraft ci --base <base>` is your finish line; to open PRs, add a GitHub repository you can push to: git remote add origin <url>``
   - `merge <n>` (with or without `--no-review "<reason>"`) checks it after the `no-review-without-reason` refusal (which stays first, as today) and before any `gh` call or fetch. It refuses `no-origin`:
     `shipcraft refused: this repository has no remote named origin, so shipcraft merge has no PR to merge`
     `Why: merge reads the PR and its statuses on GitHub through origin; nothing was fetched or sent`
     and the same `Next:` line as `pr`'s.
   - No `gh` is run, no row is written, nothing is printed on stdout.
2. **Origin you can push to.** "You can push" here means what GitHub says about the account `gh` is logged in with (`viewerPermission`), not who owns the repository and not the identity git will push with (see Known limits). When origin exists, `pr` then takes the push URLs: point 1's output, decoded as UTF-8 with invalid bytes replaced (`String::from_utf8_lossy`), split on `\n`, each line with a trailing `\r` removed and nothing else trimmed, empty lines dropped (`pushurl`, `insteadOf` and `pushInsteadOf` apply as for the push; with several `remote.origin.pushurl` entries, `git push origin` pushes to each, so each is checked). With no URL left, `pr` refuses `origin-unverified` with `<reason>` `origin has no push URL`. Then, before any fetch, push or other `gh` call, for each URL in order, `pr` runs one `gh repo view <url> --json nameWithOwner,viewerPermission` in the repository root, and stops at the first URL that does not pass, which decides the refusal below; the other URLs get no call. `<url>` is the URL with one change: when it has the form `<scheme>://<userinfo>@<rest>` (a `@` before the first `/` after `://`), the `<userinfo>@` part is removed, so a user name and password or token written there is not in `gh`'s arguments (nor in a `gh` message that echoes them); an scp-like URL (`git@github.com:owner/repo.git`) is passed as it is. No other part of the URL is changed. The JSON is read with `serde_json` (`gh::json`'s reader; on a duplicate key its last value counts). The answer for one URL decides:
   - `gh` exits 0 and prints a JSON object whose `viewerPermission` is the string `ADMIN`, `MAINTAIN` or `WRITE`: the check passes, prints nothing, and `pr` goes on exactly as today (fetch, config, `pr-not-on-branch`, push, ...).
   - `gh` exits 0 and prints a JSON object whose `viewerPermission` is any other string (`READ`, `TRIAGE`, `NONE`, `""`) or `null`: `pr` refuses `origin-not-writable`:
     `shipcraft refused: origin is <name>, where your GitHub permission is <permission>, so shipcraft pr cannot push to it`
     `Why: pr pushes the branch to origin before anything else, and a branch pushed to a repository that is not yours fails or lands in someone else's project; nothing was fetched, pushed or sent`
     ``Next: point origin's push URL at a GitHub repository you can push to, such as your fork (git remote set-url origin <url>; when git remote -v shows other push URLs, git remote set-url --push origin <url>), or keep the work local: `shipcraft ci --base <base>` is your finish line``
     `<name>` is the answer's `nameWithOwner` when it is a nonempty string, else the words `a GitHub repository`. `<permission>` is the string as `gh` gave it, or `none` when it is `""` or `null`. In `<name>`, `<permission>` and `<reason>` below, each control character (Unicode category Cc, `char::is_control`) is replaced by one space, so the refusal stays three lines. `<base>` here is `Repo::default_branch()`, the base `pr` uses today, when `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` resolves; otherwise point 1's local rule (`main`, `master`, or `<base branch>`), since no fetch has run.
   - Anything else: `gh` cannot be run, exits nonzero, prints something that is not a JSON object, or a JSON object without a `viewerPermission` key, or with one that is neither a string nor `null`. `pr` refuses `origin-unverified`:
     `shipcraft refused: shipcraft pr could not confirm that you can push to origin: <reason>`
     `Why: pr pushes only to a repository GitHub says you can write to, and every later step needs gh too; nothing was fetched, pushed or sent`
     ``Next: check that origin is a GitHub repository (git remote get-url origin) and that gh is logged in (gh auth status), then run shipcraft pr again; or keep the work local: `shipcraft ci --base <base>` is your finish line``
     `<reason>`: when `gh` could not be run or exited nonzero, the first nonempty line of the error string `gh::run` returns (stderr and stdout, each trimmed, joined by one space, then trimmed: so one-line stderr and one-line stdout make one line), trimmed, or `gh failed with no message` when there is none; when it exited 0, `gh did not return your permission on origin`. `<base>` as in the previous bullet.
   - In every refusal of this point: no fetch, no push, no other `gh` call, no row (`.git/shipcraft/runs.jsonl` byte for byte as before the command), nothing on stdout; the refusal is on stderr, exit 1, as every refusal.
   - `merge` does not run this check (point 1 only). `pr --merge` runs it once, in `pr`; its merge step does not run it again (it still runs point 1's check, which passes).
3. **The docs.** Section 7's table gains three rows, in its alphabetical order: `no-origin` (`pr` or `merge` in a repository with no remote named `origin`, item 130), `origin-not-writable` (`pr` when GitHub says your permission on origin is below write, item 130), `origin-unverified` (`pr` when `gh` cannot say whether you can push to origin, item 130). The README's requirement line "Optional, for `shipcraft pr` and `shipcraft merge`: a GitHub remote named `origin` and `gh` logged in." becomes "Optional, for `shipcraft pr` and `shipcraft merge`: a GitHub remote named `origin` and `gh` logged in; for `shipcraft pr`, also write access to `origin` for the `gh` account, which `pr` checks before it pushes anything. Without a remote, the work stays local and `shipcraft ci --base <base>` is its finish line." Nothing else in the README changes.

**Known limits.** A config with `[execution] suite_checks` makes `shipcraft ci` leave the suite to GitHub checks (item 62), so for such a project with no origin the local finish line the refusals name runs no suite; this item does not change `ci`. The check reads the permission of the `gh` account: a contributor with `WRITE` on the upstream passes and `pr` pushes there as today (contributor mode, below, is its own item), and a user who pushes with a deploy key or another SSH account while the `gh` account has `READ` is refused `origin-not-writable` (the PR could not be opened with that `gh` account either). Only `<scheme>://` userinfo is removed from the lookup's argument; a credential in a query string, and whatever git prints on a later push, are as today. `init` and `status` still say nothing about origin (run 4's other half). `merge` does not check the permission: a `gh pr merge` without it fails as today. A push URL that is not on a GitHub host (a local mirror, another forge) is refused as `origin-unverified` even when the user can push there; `pr` could not open a PR there anyway. When other remotes exist (a fork clone with `upstream`), the later `gh` calls resolve their repository as today, which may not be origin; keeping Shipcraft's files out of an upstream branch (contributor mode, POC-051 queue item 2) is its own later item. The check costs one `gh` call per `pr` run.

**Metric:** on the release, POC-051's shapes again: a repository with no remote (`pr` and `merge 1` refuse `no-origin`, exit 1, three lines); a scratch clone whose origin is `git@github.com:encode/httpx.git`, run with `GIT_SSH_COMMAND=false` so no git network call can succeed (`pr` refuses `origin-not-writable` with permission `READ`, and nothing is pushed or fetched). Over the next 5 items of Shipcraft's own flow and the adopters' `pr` runs (Hands-off, Draken): 0 refusals of this item on an origin the `gh` account can push to. Revert: a release that drops the check; nothing is written that a later binary must read.

### `pr` and `merge` open, read and merge the PR in origin's repository (item 144)

Wrong-verdict note. Since v2.0.0 (`nucleo/src/gh.rs`, commit `4f9d784`, `git tag --contains` gives `v2.0.0` as the oldest tag), every `gh` call of `pr` and `merge` leaves the choice of the GitHub repository to `gh`, while `pr` pushes the branch to origin and fetches its base from origin. In a clone with another remote, `gh` does not pick origin: with no `GH_REPO` and no `gh repo set-default`, `gh` 2.102.0 run without a terminal takes the first of its sorted remotes, and `upstream` sorts before `origin` (checked on a real clone with `origin` = `victorassisalves/shipcraft` and `upstream` = `cli/cli`: `gh api 'repos/{owner}/{repo}' --jq .full_name` printed `cli/cli`, and `gh pr list` listed `cli/cli`'s PRs; with `GH_REPO` set to origin's URL, in its `https://` and its scp-like form, the same call printed `victorassisalves/shipcraft`). So in a fork clone (origin = the user's fork, `upstream` = the project) `pr` pushes the working branch, with Shipcraft's config, locks, briefs, `AGENTS.md` block and close commits, to the fork, then lists, creates, edits and comments on the PR and posts its statuses in the upstream project; `merge <n>` reads, judges and merges the upstream project's PR `<n>`. Recorded as a later item by item 130's spec (commit `d11ab50`, 2026-11-18T20:22:43-03:00, its "Known limits": "the later `gh` calls resolve their repository as today, which may not be origin"), again by items 135 and 142's handovers. The layer that should have caught it is `pr`'s own contract (section 3: it "pushes, opens or updates the PR"): the PR was never tied to the repository the branch goes to and the base comes from, and no case ran `pr` in a clone with a second remote. A fix (`kind = fix`): opening a PR in a repository the user did not choose is a defect of `pr`'s target, not a missing feature.

**Reproduction, on main (`a0a10f9`, 2.83.0, the shared binary):** two local bare repositories, `upstream.git` and `fork.git`, both holding `main` with `app.py`; a clone with `origin` = `fork.git` (`origin/HEAD` set to `main`) and `upstream` = `upstream.git`; a branch `feat` with a commit adding `.shipcraft.toml` (`[execution] ci = "off"`, `review = "off"`) and a commit changing `app.py`. A fake `gh` on `PATH` logs its arguments and `GH_REPO`, answers `repo view` with `ADMIN`, and names the repository it acts on the way real `gh` does without a terminal (`GH_REPO`, else the `upstream` remote, else `origin`). `shipcraft pr --title t` exits 0 and prints `feat published to origin (<sha>)` and `PR #1 ... ready`; the branch reached `fork.git` with `.shipcraft.toml`; and every `gh` call after item 130's `repo view` (`pr list`, `pr create --base main --head feat`, the two `api -X POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/<sha>`, `pr comment 1`) ran with no `GH_REPO` and no repository argument, so the fake resolved each to `upstream.git`. `shipcraft merge 1` in the same clone ran `gh pr view 1 ...` the same way (upstream's PR 1). Script: `/private/tmp/item144-repro/repro.sh`. **The first RED case** is this shape with the acceptance `gh` stub: `pr` in a clone whose origin is `git@github.example144:acme/proj.git` (reaching the bare repository through the case's `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, see New cases) and which also has a remote named `upstream`; it fails on main because no `gh` call of `pr` after the `repo view` carries `GH_REPO=github.example144/acme/proj`.

**Which repository, and the options weighed.** Three were weighed:
- **(a) Name the repository on every `gh` call `pr` and `merge` make, as origin's.** The PR then always lives in the repository the base is fetched from and its config read from; a PR into another remote's repository can never be opened by `pr`. Nothing a user can do today with origin as the only GitHub remote changes, since `gh` already picks origin then.
- **(b) Refuse `pr` when the clone has a remote other than origin**, or when the base branch has no `.shipcraft.toml` (export's `export-uses-shipcraft` test, reversed), with a `Next:` naming `shipcraft export`. The first refuses every fork clone, including a fork of a project that uses Shipcraft, where a PR in the fork with Shipcraft's files is intended. The second refuses every first install: an adopter's first PR adds `.shipcraft.toml` to a base without one (item 128's line, "a first install is judged by the config it adds"), and nothing in the clone tells a first install from a contribution to a project that does not use Shipcraft.
- **(c) Both.** (b)'s costs, and once (a) holds the PR cannot reach upstream anyway, so (b) adds a refusal with no harm left to stop.

(a) is chosen. In a fork of a project that does not use Shipcraft, `pr` now opens the PR in the user's fork, where Shipcraft's files hurt no one, and the way to the upstream project stays item 135's: `shipcraft export --base <base> <branch>`, push that branch to the fork, and open the upstream PR by hand (item 142's `status` line already names `export` there).

**Origin's fetch URL, not its push URL.** `pr` fetches the base from origin (`git fetch -q origin`), reads the base's config from `origin/<base>`, and `merge` does the same; the PR's repository must be the one those come from, or the gate would judge one repository's PR by another's config. `gh`, when origin is its only remote, also names origin by its fetch URL. So the named repository is origin's fetch URL. A clone whose origin pushes to a different repository than it fetches from (a `pushurl` or `pushInsteadOf` naming another repository) keeps today's behavior on that point (Known limits).

**How it is named: `GH_REPO` and `GH_HOST`, not `--repo`.** `--repo` exists on `gh pr` subcommands but not on `gh api`, whose `{owner}/{repo}` placeholders (the statuses, the checks) `gh` fills from the same choice; `GH_REPO` covers both, and `gh`'s help for `gh api` says the placeholders come from "the repository specified in the `GH_REPO` environment variable". `gh api` sends its request to the default host (`GH_HOST`, else the logged-in default), not to `GH_REPO`'s host, so a GitHub Enterprise origin also needs `GH_HOST`. `gh` reads `GH_REPO` with its own override reader, which is narrower than git's URL grammar and skips the SSH host translation `gh` applies to remotes (an scp-like URL not starting with `git@` is read as `OWNER/REPO`; an SSH alias such as `git@work-gh:acme/proj.git` would send requests to the host `work-gh`); so Shipcraft does not pass origin's URL through: it gives `gh` the unambiguous `HOST/OWNER/REPO` form, after the same SSH translation `gh`'s remote resolver does (`ssh -G <host>`'s `hostname`, and `ssh.github.com` read as `github.com`). Every argument list `pr` and `merge` give `gh` stays byte for byte as today.

Everything in items 3, 4, 5, 10, 35, 42, 54, 62, 63, 73, 85, 96, 103, 108, 110, 115, 128, 130 and 141 holds unless a point below changes it: refusals and their order, exit codes, stdout and stderr, statuses, comments, rows, files written, and every `gh` argument list.

1. **The repository.** `pr` runs one `git remote get-url origin` in the repository root right after item 130's check passed; `merge` right after item 130's point 1 passed (git applies `insteadOf`; with several `remote.origin.url` entries it prints the first). Its stdout is decoded as UTF-8 with invalid bytes replaced, split on `\n`, and the first piece taken with exactly one trailing `\r` removed: that is `<url>`. If the git call cannot be started, ends on a signal or exits nonzero, it is a failure of shipcraft as `Repo::run` reports it (`shipcraft: error: ...`, exit 2), before any further `gh` call, push or fetch: origin exists (item 130 just saw it), so git cannot fail here without something being wrong. `<origin repo>` is then read from `<url>`, as `HOST/OWNER/REPO`:
   - `<url>` is `<scheme>://<authority>/<path>` with `<scheme>` one of `https`, `http`, `ssh`, `git`, `git+ssh` (ASCII case-insensitive), or scp-like: no `://`, and a `:` before any `/`, the text before that `:` being the authority and the text after it the path. Any other `<url>` (a local path, a `file://` URL, another scheme) gives no `<origin repo>`.
   - In the authority, everything up to and including its last `@` is dropped (userinfo); then, for the `<scheme>://` form, a final `:<digits>` is dropped (the port). What remains is `<host>`; empty, or starting with `[`, gives no `<origin repo>`.
   - For the `ssh` and `git+ssh` schemes and the scp-like form, `<host>` is translated as `gh`'s remote resolver translates it: Shipcraft runs `ssh -G <host>` (stdin from `/dev/null`, stderr discarded, `ssh` as found on `PATH`) and, when it exits 0 and prints a line `hostname <name>` with a nonempty `<name>`, `<host>` becomes the first such `<name>`; otherwise (no `ssh`, a nonzero exit, no such line) `<host>` stays as written. Then, for every form, a `<host>` equal to `ssh.github.com` (ASCII case-insensitive) becomes `github.com`, and `<host>` is lowercased.
   - The path: leading and trailing `/` removed, then a final `.git` removed; it must then be exactly two nonempty segments `<owner>/<repo>` split on `/`, else there is no `<origin repo>`.
   - `<origin repo>` is `<host>/<owner>/<repo>` and `<origin host>` is `<host>`.
   When there is no `<origin repo>`, `pr` and `merge` set no variable and their `gh` calls run as today, printing nothing about it. That is an exception to section 3's sentence, kept on purpose: such an origin is not a GitHub repository Shipcraft can name (the acceptance battery's bare paths, a mirror on another host), `pr` with such a push URL is already refused by item 130 (`gh repo view` cannot read it), and refusing `merge` there would break every local-path setup that works today.

This includes the calls of the layers `pr` runs (the review's `pr view` for the title, the statuses, the summary and review comments, the GitHub CI and check reads, the waits of items 62, 73 and 96, from whichever thread makes them), and `merge`'s `pr view`, statuses, check reads, `--no-review` comment and `pr merge`. An inherited `GH_REPO` and `GH_HOST` are replaced for those processes; every other variable is passed as today. Item 130's own `gh repo view <url>` calls run as today (they name the URL as an argument, and neither variable is set for them). Nothing else changes: no argument is added or removed, no line is printed, no row field is added, and `shipcraft`'s own environment is not changed (a suite, a build, the hook, the review agent and the `shipcraft ci --pr` child that local CI starts do not get these variables from Shipcraft; only `gh` processes that `pr` or `merge` start themselves do; that child runs as point 3's `ci`). `merge`'s success output keeps its advice-only cleanup line, with no `gh` read after the merge.

**Known limits.** `pr` never opens a PR into another repository: a contributor whose fork's PR should go upstream uses `export` and opens the upstream PR by hand, outside Shipcraft's gate. A clone whose origin pushes to another repository than it fetches from gets its PR named in the fetch repository, whose base and config `pr` reads, while the branch goes to the push repository: `gh pr create` then fails or finds a same-named branch there, as today (item 130 checks only the push URLs). `merge <pr>` given a PR URL rather than a number lets `gh` read the URL's own repository, as today: the user named it. `pr`'s lookup of an open PR (`gh pr list --head <branch>`) matches by branch name in origin's repository, so a PR from someone else's fork with the same branch name can be taken for this one, as today. `review --pr <n>`, `ci`'s GitHub reads, `status`'s protection read and `init --github` still follow `gh`'s own choice, so in a fork clone they can still read or write the upstream project (`init --github`'s protection needs admin there, so it fails for a contributor); `report --github` follows it on purpose (item 79), so in a fork clone it must run with `GH_REPO` set to origin's URL to read the PRs `pr` wrote. A user who relied on `gh repo set-default` or `GH_REPO` to send `pr`'s PR to a repository other than origin's no longer can. An origin whose URL point 1 cannot read as `HOST/OWNER/REPO` (a local path, another forge, a GitHub path with more segments) keeps `gh`'s own choice, as today. Point 1's SSH translation reads `ssh -G` as `gh` does; an SSH setup that `ssh -G` does not resolve to the API host (a `ProxyCommand`-only alias) names the alias's host, as `gh`'s own resolver would.

### Every `gh` call names origin's repository (item 151)

Wrong-verdict note. Since v2.0.0 (`nucleo/src/gh.rs`, commit `4f9d784`, where `review --pr`, `status`'s protection read, `init --github`'s protection write and `ci`'s merge check first appear; `git tag --contains 4f9d784` gives `v2.0.0` as the oldest tag), these commands leave the choice of the GitHub repository to `gh`, which in a clone with a second remote does not pick origin (item 144's note: `gh` 2.102.0 without a terminal takes the first of its sorted remotes, and `upstream` sorts before `origin`). Item 144 (2.83.1) fixed `pr` and `merge` and recorded the rest as a known limit (its spec commit `55fb8df`, 2026-11-20T14:29:36-03:00: "`review --pr <n>`, `ci`'s GitHub reads, `status`'s protection read and `init --github` still follow `gh`'s own choice"). So in a fork clone (origin = the user's fork, `upstream` = the project) `review --pr <n>` reads and judges the upstream project's PR `<n>` and posts its `shipcraft/review` status and comment there, `ci` on the default branch reads the upstream project's PRs, statuses and comments to judge escapes, `status` reports the upstream project's branch protection, and `init --github` tries to set branch protection on the upstream project. `report --github` and `report --findings` read the upstream project's PRs too, while since 2.83.1 the PR numbers in the run log are origin's. The layer that should have caught it is item 144's own spec, which fixed one class member per command it touched instead of the class (every `gh` call Shipcraft makes). A fix (`kind = fix`): reading or writing a repository the user did not choose is a defect of the call's target, not a missing feature.

**Reproduction, on main (`04f7661`, 2.89.0, the shared binary):** two local bare repositories, `fork.git` and `upstream.git`, both holding `main`; a clone of `fork.git` whose origin is then set to `git@github.example151:me/proj.git` (reaching `fork.git` through `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, a fake `ssh` printing `hostname github.example151` for `-G`) and with `upstream` = `upstream.git`; a fake `gh` on `PATH` that logs its arguments, `GH_REPO` and `GH_HOST`, and names the repository it would act on the way real `gh` does without a terminal (`GH_REPO`, else the `upstream` remote, else `origin`). `shipcraft init --github --lang other ...` runs `gh api -X PUT repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection --input <file>`; `shipcraft review --pr 1` runs `gh pr view 1 --json number,title,body,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName,isCrossRepository`; `shipcraft ci --base HEAD~1` on `main` runs `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha>/pulls`; `shipcraft status` runs `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection`; `shipcraft report --findings` runs `gh pr list --state merged --limit 1000 --json number`: every one with no `GH_REPO` and no `GH_HOST`, so the fake resolved each to `upstream`. Script: `/private/tmp/item151-repro/repro.sh <binary>`. **The first RED case** is the `review --pr` shape with the acceptance `gh` stub (item 144's harness): `review --pr 1` in a clone whose origin is `git@github.example151:acme/proj.git` and which also has a remote named `upstream`; it fails on main because its `gh pr view` carries no `GH_REPO=github.example151/acme/proj`.

**`report --github` and `report --findings` follow origin too.** Item 79 left the repository to `gh` on purpose, and gave the reason in its own text: `report --github` must read with "the same one `shipcraft pr` and `merge` made when they wrote the PR numbers". Since item 144 that choice is origin's repository whenever origin reads as one, so the same reason now says origin. Keeping `gh`'s choice would make `report` read another repository's PR of the same number in every fork clone, silently, and item 144's workaround (run it with `GH_REPO` set by hand) would be a rule only the user can apply. `report --findings` (item 121) reads the review comments that `pr` and `review --pr` posted, in the repository this item names for them. The one cost: PR numbers that a pre-2.83.1 `pr` wrote in a fork clone named the upstream project's PRs, and `report --github` now reads origin's PR of that number; such a clone can still set the repository by hand only by pointing origin at it (below), and the lock is then read wrong as it was before 2.83.1 the other way. Kept as a known limit.

**One rule for every `gh` call.** From this item on, every `gh` process Shipcraft starts gets `GH_REPO=<origin repo>` and `GH_HOST=<origin host>` (item 144's point 1 reader, unchanged, read from origin's fetch URL) whenever origin reads as one, replacing any inherited value, with exactly one exception: item 130's `gh repo view <url> --json nameWithOwner,viewerPermission`, which names the repository it checks as its argument and runs with the inherited environment, as today. When there is no `<origin repo>` (no origin remote, or a URL that point 1 of item 144 reads as none: a local path, a `file://` URL, another scheme, a path of other than two segments; for `report`, also a failed read, point 1 below), the call runs with the inherited environment: `gh`'s own choice, as today. Item 144's reader is syntactic and applies to every host: an origin on another forge (`https://gitlab.com/acme/platform.git`) reads as `gitlab.com/acme/platform`, and Shipcraft's `gh` calls then go to that host and fail, as `pr` and `merge` already do since item 144; Shipcraft does not recognize forges. No `gh` argument list changes anywhere: no `--repo`, no `-R`.

Everything in items 3, 5, 5.3, 5.5, 42, 47, 54, 62, 63, 76, 79, 121, 130, 135, 142 and 144 holds unless a point below changes it: refusals and their order, exit codes, stdout and stderr, statuses, comments, rows, files written, and every `gh` argument list.

1. **When the repository is read.** A run reads origin's repository at most once, with item 144's point 1 (one `git remote get-url origin`, then, for an `ssh`/`git+ssh`/scp-like URL, one `ssh -G <host>`), and every `gh` process it starts afterwards uses that answer:
   - `pr` and `merge` (alone or as `pr --merge`'s merge step): unchanged from item 144: right after item 130's check (for `merge`, its point 1), with a `git` failure there a failure of shipcraft (`shipcraft: error: ...`, exit 2). `pr --merge` keeps item 144's two reads (one per half).
   - Every other command that starts `gh` through `gh::run` (`review --pr <n>`, `ci`, `status`, `init --github`): right before its first `gh` process, in the repository root. A command run that starts no `gh` process runs no `git remote get-url origin`, no `git remote` and no `ssh -G` for this item (`ci` off the default branch or with nothing to check there, `init` without `--github`, `status` refused before its protection read).
   - **A failed read, for those four commands.** When that `git remote get-url origin` cannot be started, ends on a signal or exits nonzero, Shipcraft runs `git remote` once in the root. Its stdout is read as item 144's point 1 reads `get-url`'s (UTF-8, invalid bytes replaced), split on `\n`, each piece with exactly one trailing `\r` removed. If it exits 0, its output is read in full, and no piece is exactly `origin`, there is no origin remote: no `<origin repo>`, nothing printed, and the calls run with the inherited environment. Otherwise (`origin` is listed, or `git remote` cannot be started, ends on a signal, exits nonzero or its output cannot be read) the read failed, and no `gh` process is started for that call or any later call of the run: each fails as a `gh` call that could not start, with the error text `could not read origin's repository: <error>`, `<error>` being the text `Repo::run` gives for the failed `git remote get-url origin` (for a nonzero exit, `` `git remote get-url origin` failed: <its stderr, trimmed> ``). Each command then takes the path it already has for a failed `gh` call, so a repository Shipcraft could not read is never replaced by `gh`'s choice where the call writes or decides: `review --pr <n>` stops with `` shipcraft: error: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,body,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName,isCrossRepository` failed: could not read origin's repository: <error> `` on stderr, exit 2, nothing published or written; `ci`'s merge check prints `shipcraft: warning: could not check merges on <branch> through gh: could not read origin's repository: <error>` and stops checking, as for any `gh` error, and its closed-lock check (item 42) finds the squash not proved, as for any `gh` error; `status` prints `shipcraft: could not read branch protection (could not read origin's repository: <first line of error>): use \`shipcraft merge\` as the gate`; `init --github`, after its files, prints `shipcraft: could not mark statuses as required (could not read origin's repository: <error>); \`shipcraft merge\` is the gate.` (through the project's invocation, as item 146 routes it) and exits as it does after any failed protection write.
   - **Once per run.** The answer (a pair, no pair, or a failed read) is kept for the rest of the run: a run starts at most one `git remote get-url origin`, one `git remote` and one `ssh -G` for this item, however many `gh` calls follow, including runs with no pair (a local-path origin) and runs whose read failed. `pr` and `merge` set it at item 144's moment instead (`pr --merge` reads twice, once per half, as item 144 says); item 130's `repo view` neither reads it nor uses it, and never starts the read.
   - `report --github` and `report --findings` (through item 79's runner, `relatorio_gh`): right before their first `gh` process, `git remote get-url origin` runs in item 76's `<root>` with the environment item 79's `gh` calls get (the repository-selecting git variables removed, so it reads `<root>`'s origin, as `gh`'s own git calls do), stdin from `/dev/null` and stderr discarded. Any failure of it gives no `<origin repo>`, silently, and no `git remote` runs: `report` writes nothing and decides no gate, so it keeps item 79's fallback to `gh`'s choice rather than turning every call into `gh failed`. Kept once per run like the others. It is outside item 79's 60 s limit, which still covers each `gh` call. `report` without `--github` or `--findings` starts no `gh` and runs no such read.
   - `ssh -G <host>`, in every command, runs exactly as item 144's point 1 runs it (in `shipcraft`'s own working directory and environment, stdin `/dev/null`, stderr discarded).
2. **Which calls.** The call sites in the code, each with the rule it follows:
   - **Origin's repository (this item's rule):**
     - `pr` (`nucleo/src/pr.rs`, through `nucleo/src/gh.rs`): `pr list --head <branch> --state open --json number,body`; `pr create ...`; `pr edit <n> ...` (title, body); `pr view <n> --json title`; `api -X POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/<sha> ...` (`shipcraft/ci`, `shipcraft/review`); `api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha>/statuses`; item 62's check reads (`api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha>/check-runs?...` and `.../commits/<sha>/status?per_page=100`), the waits of items 62, 73 and 96 included; `pr comment <n> --body-file <file>` (summary, review comment). Read at item 144's moment.
     - `merge <pr>` (`nucleo/src/merge.rs`): `pr view <n> --json number,state,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName`; the statuses read; item 62's check reads; the `--no-review` comment; `pr merge <n> --<method> --match-head-commit <sha>`. Read at item 144's moment.
     - `review --pr <n>` (`pr::of_pr` and its publishing): `pr view <n> --json number,title,body,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName,isCrossRepository`; the `shipcraft/review` statuses (pending, reused, final); `pr comment <n>`. Changed: read before the `pr view`.
     - `ci` on the default branch, through `ci::pr_gate`, from both its callers: `ci::warn_merges` (item 5.5's escape warning, after the suites) and `ci::squash_proved` (item 42: a commit arriving on the default branch with a lock already closed is admitted when its PR's gate is proved, read before the suites): `api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha>/pulls`, `api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<head>/statuses`, `api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/<n>/comments`. Changed.
     - `status` (`merge::status`): `api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/<base>/protection`. Changed.
     - `init --github` (`init::protect`): `api -X PUT repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/<branch>/protection --input <file>`. Changed.
     - `report --github` and `report --findings` (`nucleo/src/relatorio_gh/`, item 79's runner): every call they make (`pr view`, the paginated status and check-run reads, the Blocking-count and findings reads, `pr list`). Changed.
   - **The repository named in the arguments (inherited environment):** item 130's `gh repo view <url> --json nameWithOwner,viewerPermission` (`origin::check_pr`), the only `gh` call Shipcraft makes outside the rule above.
   - No other command starts `gh` (`export`, `uninstall`, `red`, `check`, `close`, the local `review`, `--version` and usage start none). Every `gh` process goes through one of two runners, `gh::run` (`nucleo/src/gh.rs`) and `relatorio_gh::process::run`; a later `gh` call follows this item's rule by going through either runner, and a new exception must be named in this list.
3. **The environment otherwise.** Only `gh` processes get the two variables; `shipcraft`'s own environment does not change (a suite, a build, the hook, the review agent and the `shipcraft ci --pr` child that `pr`'s local CI starts get nothing from this item; that child reads origin itself under point 1 when it starts `gh`). Every other variable a `gh` process gets stays as today (item 79's `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` and its removed git variables included).
4. **A user who chose the repository on purpose.** `GH_REPO` set in the environment, or `gh repo set-default`, no longer redirects any Shipcraft `gh` call whose origin reads as a repository: `GH_REPO` is replaced for that process, and `gh` reads `GH_REPO` before its default, so the default is not consulted either. To make Shipcraft read or write another repository, point origin's fetch URL at it (`git remote set-url origin <url>`), or work in a clone whose origin is that repository. With no origin remote, or an origin URL that does not read as a repository (a local path, a `file://` URL, a path of other than two segments), both still choose, as today; an origin on another forge reads as a repository of that host (above), so they do not choose there. Item 130's `repo view` still follows the URL it is given.
5. **Section 3.** After the command table, after the line ``init` writes no run-log row; `red` and `close` write one each (item 38).``, the spec gains the paragraph ``Every `gh` call a command makes names origin's repository (`GH_REPO` and `GH_HOST`) when origin's fetch URL reads as one, except item 130's `gh repo view <url>`, which names the URL it checks (item 151).`` Nothing else in section 3, the README, the briefs, the `AGENTS.md` block or section 7 changes. Item 144's point 3 ("What does not change") and the part of its Known limits naming `review --pr`, `ci`, `status`, `init --github` and `report --github` are superseded by this item, and so is one sentence of item 121's point 2, "No git subprocess runs": `report --findings` now runs point 1's one `git remote get-url origin` in `<root>` (and, for an SSH-form URL, one `ssh -G`) before its first `gh` call, and no other git; its root discovery and everything else of item 121 stay.

**Known limits.** `merge <pr>` and `review --pr <pr>` given a PR URL rather than a number let `gh` read the URL's own repository, as today (the user named it). A clone whose origin fetches from one repository and pushes to another names the fetch repository, as item 144 does. PR numbers that a pre-2.83.1 `pr` wrote in a fork clone belong to the upstream project, and `report --github` now reads origin's PR of that number. `review --pr <n>` still fetches `refs/pull/<n>/head` from origin, now the same repository its `pr view` read (before, a fork clone read upstream's PR and fetched the fork's ref). The `git remote get-url origin` read of `report` is outside item 79's 60 s limit. An SSH setup that `ssh -G` does not resolve to the API host names the alias's host, as item 144 says.

**Metric:** on the release, with real `gh`, read-only: a clone with `origin` = `git@github.com:victorassisalves/shipcraft.git` and `upstream` = `https://github.com/cli/cli.git`; `shipcraft status` prints the protection line of `victorassisalves/shipcraft`'s `main`, and `shipcraft report --findings --json` lists this repository's findings, not `cli/cli`'s (a `gh` wrapper logs `GH_REPO=github.com/victorassisalves/shipcraft` on each call and passes only `api` GETs and `pr list`/`pr view` to the real `gh`). Over the next 5 items of Shipcraft's flow and the adopters' runs (Hands-off, Draken; origin their only GitHub remote): 0 failures this item causes. Revert: a release where `gh::run` reads no repository unless `pr` or `merge` pinned one, and `relatorio_gh` reads none; nothing is written that a later binary must read.
